Damn it—last night I was drinking with the neighbor, Old Wang, and we talked about compliance and privacy. He shut me down on the spot so hard I couldn’t even speak. This guy had been working on a compliance project recently. To satisfy financial regulation, he spent three whole months tuning a third-party KYC interface. In the end, the customer’s identity privacy leaked—he almost got fined by the regulator to the point of financial ruin! At that moment I thought: in this space, there are so many “Layer 1 privacy chains built for financial compliance.” Is there actually one that’s any good?

Fine, I decided to take out my laptop and put Dusk Network through real testing. Dusk always claims it’s the king of privacy compliance for tokenizing financial assets. It pushes two core selling points: one is the Confidential Smart Contract standard (XSC), and the other is the Citadel KYC identity system based on zero-knowledge proofs. @Dusk_Foundation 

Yeah, the marketing hype is off the charts, so I went straight to try it. Most tutorials only teach you basic transfers, but what many people don’t know is that when Dusk’s custom Piecrust virtual machine runs zero-knowledge proof computations, it places extremely strict constraints on how the underlying node state updates. I even wrote a test smart contract that calls Citadel to perform identity verification. Supposedly, as long as you can generate a zero-knowledge proof proving I’m over 18 and on the whitelist, you can get authorization right away without ever exposing my real ID number. #ETH 

So guess what? In actual deployment testing, Dusk’s privacy compliance truly has its own unique approach. In Citadel’s architecture, the encrypted license (License) is directly attached to the Merkle tree. Users can put the required authorization on-chain by presenting only a Hash proof. This both meets regulators’ traceability requirements for financial institutions and keeps data security in the user’s own hands. Honestly, it’s way smarter than the traditional “data-moving” style of KYC.

I feel like I stepped into every single one of the pitfalls. Dusk’s mechanism of “compliant privacy plus high performance” results in zero-knowledge proof generation being extremely resource-intensive for the local client. When I ran a node on a low-end VPS and tried generating test proofs, the CPU jumped straight to 100%—and at one point transactions even got stuck. If high-frequency financial businesses come along later, can ordinary users’ mobile devices handle this kind of local ZK generation cost? I really have my doubts.

I think Dusk Network is taking an extremely niche but also very hardcore path, and it’s hard
#dusk $DUSK

卧槽，昨晚跟隔壁老王喝酒聊到合规隐私，我当场被他怼得哑口无言。这哥们前阵子做合规项目，为了搞定金融监管，整整调了三个月第三方KYC接口，结果客户身份隐私泄漏，差点被监管罚到倾家荡产！我当时就想，现在这圈子里喊着“为金融合规而生”的Layer 1隐私链多如牛毛，到底有没有能打的？
服了，我干脆自己掏出笔记本实战测一下 Dusk Network。Dusk 这项目天天宣传自己是搞金融资产Token化的隐私合规王者，主打两大核心卖点：一个是保密智能合约标准（XSC），另一个就是基于零知识证明的 Citadel KYC身份系统。@Dusk_Foundation 

哎呀，吹得天花乱坠，我直接去搞体验。很多教程都只教你简单的转账，但大家不太知道的是，Dusk 自研的 Piecrust 虚拟机在跑零知识证明计算的时候，对底层节点状态更新有极其苛刻的约束！我自己写了个测试合约，调用 Citadel 去做身份证明验证。按理说，只要生成零知识证明证明我满18岁且在白名单，就能直接通过授权，根本不用泄露我的真实身份证号。#ETH 

结果你猜怎么着？在实际部署测试时，Dusk 的隐私合规确实有独到之处。在 Citadel 架构里，加密许可（License）直接挂在 Merkle 树上，用户出示一个 Hash 证明就能上链，既满足了金融机构的监管追溯，又把数据安全握在自己手里，这点确实比传统数据搬家式的KYC高明太多。

我认为坑爹的地方我给踩了个遍！Dusk 这种“既要合规隐私，又要高性能”的机制，导致零知识证明生成极其消耗本地客户端性能。我在低配 VPS 上跑节点并尝试生成测试证明时，CPU直接飙到100%，甚至一度把交易挂起。这要是以后高频金融业务上来，普通用户的移动端设备能不能抗住这种本地 ZK 生成成本？真得打个问号。

我觉得，Dusk Network 走的是一条极其偏门但也极其硬核的道路，很难

After the release of macro data, the probability of a September rate hike by the Federal Reserve falls to about 33%

After a series of recent U.S. macroeconomic data releases, Wall Street traders have significantly adjusted their bets on the Fed’s near-term policy path. According to reports citing data from the CME Group “FedWatch” tool, the market-implied probability of a rate hike at the September FOMC meeting has dropped to around 33%. Meanwhile in the early hours of August 20 Beijing time, the Fed will release the minutes from the July FOMC meeting. Chicago Fed President Goolsbee said that the recent cooling of inflation is encouraging, and he expects that data in the coming months will continue to improve to confirm that inflation is returning to the 2% target. Together, the above information forms the main backdrop for the repricing of current interest-rate expectations.

In terms of event context, the Fed’s interest-rate decisions have long been an important anchor for global asset pricing. Traders use instruments such as federal funds futures to translate their views on economic growth, inflation stickiness, and employment conditions into tradable probabilities. CME FedWatch-type tools are based on related futures pricing and reflect the market’s implied odds that the Federal Open Market Committee will keep, raise, or lower the federal funds target rate at its next meeting. What needs to be clearly distinguished is that tool readings are the result of market trading—not an official commitment by the Fed, nor a guarantee of the final decision. They can move quickly with incoming data, officials’ remarks, and risk events.

The core facts can be summarized in three points. First, after this week’s macro data release, traders sharply cut their bets on a September rate hike, corresponding to a probability falling to about one-third. Second, with the July meeting minutes about to be released, the market hopes to glean from them internal discussion details by the committee regarding inflation, growth, and the policy timetable. Third, Goolsbee’s latest remarks focusing on the trend of easing inflation, along with his emphasis that data in the coming months needs to continue to confirm a return to the 2% target, echoes the pricing direction of “lower urgency for near-term hikes.” All of the above are facts at the level of information that has already been disclosed, and they do not involve assertions about the outcome of the decision.

In terms of logic, a decline in the rate-hike probability usually corresponds to a few observable conditions: inflation readings show signs of easing; growth or demand indicators no longer support the need for further tightening right away; and some regional Fed officials place greater emphasis on patience and data dependence. A drop from a higher probability level to about 33% suggests that the trading book has shifted from “more likely to act” to “more likely to hold,” but the remaining roughly 30% probability also indicates that a September rate hike has not been fully ruled out. If the minutes’ text shows continued concern about inflation stickiness or heightened caution about external shocks, the probability could rise again; conversely, if the minutes reinforce a wait-and-see consensus, existing pricing may become even more solid. Individual officials’ speeches can carry signal value, but they are not sufficient to represent the committee’s overall stance; continuous data and remarks from multiple committee members remain more critical.

The transmission path to the crypto market mainly runs through three channels: liquidity expectations, real-rate narratives, and risk appetite—rather than a linear mapping from a single probability number. When the market lowers the probability of a near-term rate hike, it often implies a marginal easing of concerns about further tightening; dollar funding conditions and global risk-asset sentiment may improve in tandem. Mainstream crypto assets such as Bitcoin and Ethereum, as high-volatility risk assets, have historically tended to react to shifts in the direction of rate expectations. When expectations cool, a repair in risk appetite helps funds recover their risk budgets; if subsequent data repeatedly revives concerns about inflation as meeting minutes turn more hawkish or external shocks trigger renewed re-inflation worries, expectations could quickly reverse and crypto asset volatility would likely amplify accordingly. It is crucial to separate facts from speculation: the facts are that the current September rate-hike probability is about 33%, that the minutes will be released, and that Goolsbee mentioned the cooling of inflation; the speculation is that “the probability drop will inevitably lead to sustained gains” or that “the crypto market has already priced everything in”—the latter has no supporting evidence and can only be treated as scenario discussion.

Our editorial take and observation are as follows: we are currently on the eve of a window packed with data and text, so the decline in readings looks more like traders’ immediate reaction to recent macro cues rather than a conclusion that the policy cycle has already turned. A probability of about 33% means “hold steady” is becoming the more mainstream baseline scenario, but event risk remains—especially the wording in the meeting minutes, subsequent inflation and employment data, and external variables such as energy that could affect prices. For participants in the crypto market, it is more valuable to track whether rate-expectation expectations are stable, whether dollar liquidity expectations are improving in sync, and whether linkages among risk assets are consistent—rather than interpreting a single probability fluctuation as a trend-reversal signal. Overall, this repricing adjustment provides conditions for sentiment to ease, but the medium-term direction still depends on subsequent verification, not on the probability shift by itself.

从事件背景看，美联储利率决策长期是全球资产定价的重要锚。交易员通过联邦基金期货等工具，把对经济增长、通胀粘性与就业状况的判断转化为可交易的概率。芝商所FedWatch一类工具，正是基于相关期货定价，反映市场对联邦公开市场委员会下一次会议维持、上调或下调联邦基金目标利率的隐含概率。需要明确区分的是：工具读数是市场交易结果，不是美联储官方承诺，更不是对最终决议的保证；它会随数据、官员讲话和风险事件快速波动。

核心事实可以归纳为三点。第一，在本周宏观数据公布后，交易员大幅削减9月加息押注，对应概率回落至约三分之一的水平。第二，7月会议纪要即将披露，市场希望从中观察委员会对通胀、增长与政策节奏的内部讨论细节。第三，古尔斯比的最新表态 devoting 于通胀降温趋势，并强调需要未来数月数据继续确认向2%目标回归，这与“短期加息紧迫性下降”的定价方向形成呼应。以上内容均属于已披露信息层面的事实，不涉及对决议结果的断言。

逻辑拆解上，加息概率下降通常对应几类可观察条件：通胀读数出现缓和、增长或需求指标不再支持立即进一步收紧、以及部分地区联储官员更强调耐心与数据依赖。概率从更高水平回落至约33%，说明交易盘口已从“更可能动”转向“更可能不动”，但约三成的剩余概率也表明，9月加息并未被完全排除。纪要文本若显示对通胀粘性的持续担忧，或对外部冲击的警惕，仍可能令概率再度抬升；反之，若纪要强化观望共识，现有定价可能进一步稳固。官员个人讲话有信号意义，但不足以代表委员会整体立场，连续数据与多位委员表态仍更关键。

对加密市场的影响路径，主要经由流动性预期、实际利率叙事和风险偏好三条渠道，而非单一概率数字的线性映射。当市场下调短期加息概率时，往往意味着对政策进一步收紧的担忧边际缓解，美元融资条件与全球风险资产情绪可能同步改善。比特币、以太坊等主流加密资产作为高弹性风险品种，历史上常对利率预期的方向变化作出反应：预期缓和时，风险偏好修复有助于资金风险预算回升；若后续数据反复、纪要偏鹰或外部冲击推高再通胀担忧，则预期可能迅速回调，加密资产波动也会随之放大。必须把事实与推测分开：事实是当前9月加息概率约33%、纪要将公布、古尔斯比提及通胀降温；推测是“概率回落必然带来持续上涨”或“加密市场已定价完毕”——后者并无证据支持，只能作为情景讨论。

编辑判断与观察是：当前处在数据与文本密集窗口前夜，读数回落更像交易员对近期宏观线索的即时反应，而不是政策周期已经转向的定论。约33%的概率意味着“按兵不动”成为更主流的基准情形，但事件风险仍在，尤其是会议纪要措辞、后续通胀与就业数据，以及能源等可能影响物价的外部变量。对加密市场参与者而言，更有价值的是跟踪利率预期是否稳定、美元流动性预期是否同步改善，以及风险资产之间的联动是否一致，而不是把单次概率波动解读为趋势翻转信号。总体而言，此次预期调整提供了情绪缓和的条件，但中期方向仍取决于后续验证，而非一次盘口变化本身。

A few days ago I went through Dusk’s core, privacy, and settlement from top to bottom—yet today I’m stalled by a rather small issue: which door does the average person walk through?

In the past, the Dusk Web Wallet was more like an independent service counter. You can do things like transfers and staking there, but it doesn’t sit on the same corridor as the outside dApps. If an app wants to find a wallet, request an account, or have the user sign a transaction, it can’t simply reuse a single unified interface. For developers, onboarding each additional wallet can mean writing another round of compatibility code; for users, it means yet another page jump, learning new buttons, and wondering whether they’ve walked through the wrong door.#ETH  

Dusk Connect precisely fills this unobtrusive door handle. It lets browser apps discover compatible wallets, request account access, and hand off user-approved actions to the wallet to complete. Developers don’t have to lock their apps to one specific wallet, and users don’t have to learn a fresh connection method for every dApp.

At the same time, the newly opened preview of the Dusk Wallet is set to cover browser extensions, desktop, and mobile. Public and private transfers, shield/unshield, staking, claiming rewards, asset operations, and dApp permissions are all brought into a single wallet entry point. At least from a product perspective, once Dusk starts delivering on the ability for the chain to run, the next lesson is whether people can use it conveniently—“smoothly,” right out of the gate.#BTC  

Honestly, I think this is easier to validate than adding yet another grand RWA partnership. Once wallets and Connect truly move into more apps, we’ll be able to see whether users have to click through too much, whether the permissions are understandable, and whether they can recover themselves after a failure—then we’ll know whether this door is truly built.

They’re still developer previews right now, and I won’t turn the preview version into a mature product. But if Dusk’s impressive privacy and settlement capabilities ultimately end up being accessible only to a small group of technical users, then even the best back kitchen can’t put good dishes on the table. Infrastructure is there to pave the road; the wallet is there to make people willing to walk in.

When you try a new chain, at what step are you most likely to give up: creating a wallet, connecting to an app, or the first time you sign a message?#dusk  $DUSK  @Dusk_Foundation

前几天我把 Dusk 的底层、隐私和结算翻了个遍，今天却被一个很小的问题卡住：普通人到底从哪扇门进去？

以前的 Dusk Web Wallet 更像一间独立办事厅。转账、质押这些事情能办，但它和外面的 dApp 不在同一条走廊。应用想找钱包、申请账户或者让用户签一笔交易，不能直接沿用一套统一接口。对开发者来说，每接一个钱包都可能多写一套适配；对用户来说，就是又一次跳页面、认新按钮、怀疑自己是不是走错门。#ETH  

Dusk Connect 补的正是这块不起眼的门把手。它让浏览器应用能发现兼容钱包、申请账户访问，并把需要用户批准的操作交给钱包完成。开发者不必把应用绑死在某一个钱包上，用户也不用为了每个 dApp 学一套新的连接方式。

同时开放预览的新 Dusk Wallet，则准备覆盖浏览器扩展、桌面和移动端。公开与保密转账、shield/unshield、质押、领取奖励、资产操作和 dApp 权限，都放进同一个钱包入口。至少从产品思路看，Dusk 开始补上“链能运行”之后的下一课：人能不能顺手地用。#BTC  

我反而觉得，这件事比再加一个宏大的 RWA 合作更容易检验。等钱包和 Connect 真正进入更多应用后，看看用户连接一次要点几下、权限能否看懂、失败后能不能自己恢复，就知道这扇门到底装好了没有。

目前它们仍是 developer preview，我不会把预览版写成成熟产品。但如果 Dusk 惊艳的隐私与结算能力最后只能被少数技术用户摸到，再好的后厨也端不出菜。基础设施负责把路修好，钱包负责让人愿意走进来。

你体验一条新链时，最容易在哪一步放弃：创建钱包、连接应用，还是第一次签名？

Last week I was gnawing on a cold mantou while staring at my computer, revising engineering drawings, when—out of nowhere—a liquidation alert popped up on the screen through a chain link. I was so mad I almost laughed. Recently I saw a lot of hype around TermMax, a decentralized fixed-rate protocol built on a fixed-rate basis. The marketing said it could handle fixed-income and options trading with high capital efficiency—top-tier, sky-high claims. I even went in with a few ETH to run some tests. After actually using it, the pros and cons were both pretty glaring—it’s definitely not as miraculous as the marketing accounts make it sound. @termmax 
The TMX’s most core marketing highlight is the integration of fixed-rate and options: it uses a zero-coupon bond token model. I went through the interactions step by step and found that TermMax does have something in its matching mechanism. When using it for fixed-rate borrowing/lending, since it turns the yield to maturity into standardized assets, the capital utilization ratio really is much higher than those old-school lending protocols. But when I got into deep operations, I found a “deadly flaw” that most people hardly notice: when you try to set up large notional options-hedging combinations inside TermMax, the underlying AMM liquidity pool liquidity can cause slippage to become wildly outrageous during liquidity gaps. I thought my orders would perfectly eat the fixed-income side, but in reality the implied volatility matched was off by a whole lot compared with what the interface estimated—almost enough to wipe out the expected yield. I was just fed up. #ETH 
Let me share another detail that many people don’t catch: TermMax’s frontend looks smooth, but when it calls Oracle price feeds and then matches the option contracts, on-chain gas consumption becomes inexplicably higher during certain time windows. I specifically tracked on-chain data—the TMX contract call path is too long in the logic that triggers liquidation under multiple collateralization. That means when the market moves hard, small retail traders trying to manually close positions early find it extremely painful: if your reaction time is a bit slow, you get trapped.
Anyway, stepping aside from all these pitfalls, TermMax’s attempt at decentralized fixed-rate trading is indeed a novel breakthrough in the industry. Whether TMX can truly run depends entirely on whether it can make the liquidity pools on the second layer genuinely deeper, and whether it can optimize that bulky liquidation logic. Don’t just listen to hype—when playing with protocols like this, you must personally take the time to dismantle its underlying hedging path with small amounts of capital. If you have your head clear, you won’t get cut. #termmax

TMX最核心的宣传亮点是做固定利率和期权整合，用的是零息债券Token模式。我当时一步步去交互体验，发现TermMax在撮合机制上确实有点东西，拿去质押做固定借贷的时候，由于它把到期收益率做成了标准化资产，资金利用率确实比以前那些老牌借贷协议高不少。但我特么在深度操作的时候发现了一个大家很少注意到的死穴：当你尝试在TermMax里面做大额期权对冲组合的时候，它的底层AMM流动性池子在流动性断层时滑点大得离谱。我当时填单子的时候以为能完美吃下固定收益，结果实际匹配到的隐含波动率比界面预估的差了整整一大截，差点把预期的收益率全扣光，简直服了。#ETH 
再讲个很多人没发现的细节，TermMax前端页面看起挺丝滑，但在调取Oracle价格喂线和撮合撮合到期合约时，链上Gas消耗会在特定时间段莫名其妙偏高。我专门追了追链上数据，TMX在多重抵押清算触发的逻辑里，合约调用路径过于冗长，这就导致大行情来的时候，小散户想提前手动平仓极其痛苦，手速慢一点就直接被套牢。

If you’re already in, congratulations. If you’re not, to be honest I recommend watching for now—don’t FOMO.

ACE is also worth discussing. Fusionist, this AAA game project, is up +39% in 24 hours, with volume of 364M. But pay attention: the funding rate is -0.2997%, and shorts are overheating. My personal interpretation of this signal is that there’s a lot of disagreement in the market—some think the gaming sector can really take off, while others are borrowing coins to dump and smash the market. If this negative funding rate keeps expanding, there might be a chance for a rebound driven by short covering. But the uncertainty in the gaming sector is too high, so I lean toward observing or testing with a light position.

Now let’s talk about the decliners. CYS -38.92%, VELVET -32.88%, BEAT -29.04%. Honestly, these drawdowns are painful to look at. Especially BEAT: it has a positive funding rate of 0.0225%, yet the price got hammered like this. That’s a classic “good news used up, turned into bad news.” That’s just how daily altcoin life goes—when they rally you can’t catch up, and when they fall you can’t escape.

On the trending search list, GPS, PENGU, PUMP, MON, and HYPE all have buzz. Pudgy Penguins, a kind of NFT project, is trending too. I guess it might be preparing to issue a token or has some new developments. Keeping an eye on it can’t hurt.

Finally, a few trading thoughts.

BTC is currently ranging in the 63–64K zone. The 7-day trend is a bit weak, but there are signs of stabilization within the last 24 hours. If it can hold above 63K, I personally think a small rebound wave toward 65K–66K is possible, with a stop loss below 62.5K.

ETH is relatively stronger. 1,880–1,900 is a good observation range. If it can hold above 1,900, upside should open up to around 1,950 without a big problem.

For altcoins: if ACE’s negative funding rate keeps getting worse, there may be a technical rebound—but keep your position size within 5%. After all, the volatility of gaming tokens isn’t something everyone can handle. For something like GPS that has already run hard, don’t try to be the last one to get on the ride.

To be honest, the market right now feels like what it’s like on Friday night when you don’t know what to do—direction is unclear, but opportunities are always left for people with patience. Don’t rush into trading. First get clarity before you act. In the crypto space, the one thing it never lacks is opportunities—it’s your principal (capital) that it lacks.

大饼BTC在63,755附近晃悠，24小时涨了1%，7天反而跌了1.9%。怎么说呢，就是那种"涨了又好像没涨"的感觉，像极了周末加班没加班费的心情。ETH倒是稍微争气点，1,905的位置，24h +1.3%，7天几乎持平，稳得一批。恐惧贪婪指数50，Neutral，说实话这个数值就很玄学，市场既没有FOMO也没恐慌，就卡在中间当墙头草。

但是兄弟们，真正的戏不在BTC和ETH，在山寨。

GPS直接起飞，24小时拉了64%！量能443M USDT，这可不是小打小闹。GoPlus这个项目主打Web3用户安全，说实话赛道是好的，毕竟这个圈子最缺的就是安全。但我得说，这种涨幅追高需谨慎，尤其量能虽然大，但资金费率没显示，咱也别问我是怎么知道的，我就是觉得这种直线拉升往往不是给我们上车的机会，而是给持币者发红包的时刻。如果你已经在了，恭喜；如果你不在，说实话我建议看戏为主，别FOMO。

ACE也值得聊，Fusionist这个AAA游戏项目，24小时+39%，量能364M。但注意了，资金费率-0.2997%，空头过热。这个信号我个人的理解是：市场分歧很大，有人觉得游戏赛道能起来，有人在借币砸盘。Personally，这个负费率如果继续扩大，可能会有一波空头回补的反弹机会，但游戏赛道的不确定性太高，我倾向于观望或者轻仓试探。

再说说跌幅榜，CYS -38.92%，VELVET -32.88%，BEAT -29.04%。说实话，这种跌幅看着就肉疼。尤其BEAT，资金费率还有0.0225%的正费率，结果价格砸成这样，典型的"利好出尽变利空"。山寨币的日常就是这样，涨的时候你追不上，跌的时候你躲不开。

热搜榜上GPS、PENGU、PUMP、MON、HYPE都有热度。Pudgy Penguins这种NFT项目上热搜，我猜可能是要发币或者有什么新动向，关注一下没坏处。

最后给点交易思路吧。BTC目前在63-64K区间震荡，7天趋势偏弱但24小时有企稳迹象。如果接下来能守住63K，我个人觉得可以看一个反弹到65K-66K的小波段，止损放62.5K下方。ETH相对强势，1,880-1,900是不错的观察区间，如果能站稳1,900，上方空间打开到1,950问题不大。

山寨方面，ACE如果负费率继续加深，可能会有一波技术性反弹，但仓位控制在5%以内就好，毕竟游戏币的波动率不是每个人都能扛住的。GPS这种已经拉完的，就别去当那个最后接棒的人了。

说实话，现在的市场状态就像周五晚上不知道该干嘛的你——方向不明，但机会总是留给有耐心的人。别急着操作，先看清楚再动手，币圈最不缺的就是机会，缺的是本金。

🚨 JPMorgan Suddenly Accepts BTC and ETH as Collateral? Has Wall Street Really Changed?

Group: [点击进入玖玖的粉丝群](https://app.binance.com/uni-qr/VTAuSrs8)
JPMorgan is allowing institutional clients to use Bitcoin and Ethereum as collateral for USD loans.📢
What does this mean?
Crypto assets—once viewed by some traditional financial institutions as high-risk—are gradually finding their way into the collateral systems of mainstream banks.
And the real point to watch isn’t simply that “JPMorgan has started to recognize Bitcoin.”👀
More importantly, Bitcoin and Ethereum are slowly evolving from merely investment assets into assets that can participate in financing within the traditional financial system.

In simple terms:
Previously, if you held BTC, you mainly focused on price fluctuations.
Now, institutions can place BTC and ETH into custody systems and then use them to obtain USD financing through collateral.💰
Behind this is the further blurring of the boundary between crypto assets and traditional finance.
Also, JPMorgan isn’t directly putting these crypto assets into its own wallet.

The related assets are stored by a third-party custodian, the bank issues the loans, and prices are continuously assessed in real time via infrastructure such as oracles.
In other words, a “bank-style financial infrastructure” centered around crypto assets is being formed.
But there’s one very critical question here.

⚠️ Using Bitcoin as collateral doesn’t mean the bank will lend you at 100% of its value.
Because crypto prices can swing significantly, collateral is typically discounted.
For example, BTC worth $100,000 might only translate to a loan limit of around $50,000 to $70,000.

That’s actually easy to understand.
What banks fear most isn’t whether BTC has value, but whether the price suddenly drops sharply.
If the collateral value falls quickly, it could trigger margin calls—or even forced liquidation.
So this is essentially a double-edged sword.📊

On one hand, it gives institutions more reasons to hold BTC.
Because BTC isn’t just waiting for appreciation—it can also become part of corporate financing and liquidity management.

摩根大通正在允许机构客户将比特币和以太坊作为美元贷款的抵押品。📢
这意味着什么？
曾经被部分传统金融机构视为高风险资产的加密资产，如今正在逐渐进入传统银行的抵押品体系。
而真正值得关注的，并不是“摩根大通开始认可比特币”这么简单。👀
更重要的是，比特币和以太坊正在从单纯的投资资产，慢慢变成一种可以参与传统金融体系融资的资产。

简单来说：
以前你持有BTC，主要关注的是价格涨跌。
现在，机构可以把BTC、ETH放进托管体系，再通过抵押获得美元融资。💰这背后意味着加密资产与传统金融之间的边界，正在进一步模糊。而且摩根大通并不是直接把这些加密资产放进自己的钱包。

相关资产由第三方托管机构负责保管，银行负责贷款，价格则通过预言机等基础设施进行实时评估。也就是说，一套围绕加密资产的“银行式金融基础设施”正在形成。但这里还有一个非常关键的问题。

⚠️ 比特币作为抵押品，并不代表银行愿意按照100%的价值给你贷款。由于加密资产价格波动较大，抵押品通常需要打折。
例如价值10万美元的BTC，最终能够获得的贷款额度可能只有5万到7万美元左右。

这其实很好理解。
银行最担心的不是BTC有没有价值，而是价格突然大幅波动。
如果抵押品价格快速下跌，就可能触发追加抵押，甚至出现强制算。
所以这件事情其实是一把“双刃剑”。📊

一方面，它让机构持有BTC的理由变多了。
因为BTC不只是等待上涨，还可以成为企业融资和流动性管理的一部分。

Goldman Sachs bought another $386 million worth of Strategy stock, bringing its total holdings to $558 million: this time it’s not investing in the company—it’s a covert way to stock up on BTC

Goldman Sachs has significantly increased its position in Strategy stock to $558 million, with institutions using securities accounts to indirectly allocate to Bitcoin.

Goldman Sachs has newly purchased $386 million worth of Strategy (formerly MicroStrategy) stock, bringing its total holdings to $558 million. Put simply, Goldman isn’t buying coins directly on the exchange; instead, it gains BTC exposure by holding shares of this coin-hoarding company. For institutions, this route doesn’t require managing wallets or custody themselves, compliance costs are lower, and on the books it looks just like an ordinary equity position. With BTC trading around $63,822, demand for this kind of indirect exposure is clearly on the rise.

One-sentence translation: The money didn’t directly enter to buy coins, but it has already slipped in through the back door.

Impact on the market
- Short term: A sentiment tailwind. News of institutional adding will give the market a signal that “smart money is still buying.” BTC $63,822 (24h +1.14%), ETH $1,907.92 (24h +1.31%) are currently moving relatively steadily; this news adds kindling for the bulls. But note: it’s stocks, not spot, so it doesn’t directly push the price.
- Medium term: The larger the scale of these indirect holdings, the tighter the link between Strategy shares and BTC—effectively adding leverage to BTC demand for the market. If more major banks follow, “institutional allocation” could evolve from a story into a trend.

My take
Clearly bullish. Institutions are casting votes with real money; $558 million isn’t just for show. As long as BTC holds around the $63,822 area—and doesn’t break down below the prior low zone—structural buying should keep accumulating, and the probability of an upside move in the medium term is higher. The risk is that if the Strategy share premium compresses, it could amplify volatility in the opposite direction, and that’s something to watch.

Then traders care most about things like: will slippage be manageable, can orders get filled promptly, and after you cancel, how long until the order is truly invalid?

TermMax’s fixed rates do remove part of the risk like “funding rates suddenly going crazy,” but the risk hasn’t disappeared—it’s just moved to a different place. Rates are locked, but the execution price isn’t. No wild funding-rate jumping doesn’t mean you won’t get liquidity being trampled.

Over the past couple of days, I’ve gone through all of @TermMax’s documentation carefully. My biggest takeaway isn’t “fixed-rate finally has someone doing it.” It’s a different issue: when TermMax “fixes” the rate, is it fixing only the interest rate, or is it also giving users the illusion that the risk is “fixed” and locked in?

TermMax’s most attractive design is pretty straightforward: it locks in borrowing costs upfront, and at FT maturity it’s redeemed for a fixed value. That sounds comfortable—until you dig into the liquidation mechanism and realize it’s not that simple. The official documentation itself states that, in extreme market conditions, if liquidation isn’t fully executed, FT holders may receive not just the original assets that were borrowed, but a proportional share of the collateral. Moreover, the collateral value may even be insufficient to fully cover principal and interest.

This creates the main contradiction I think is worth discussing: the yield is fixed, but the underlying credit and the liquidation outcome are not fixed.

Looking further into the permission layer gets even more interesting. In a given Market, the core parameters—collateral assets, maturity date, LLTV, whether leverage is enabled, and so on—are configured by TermMax administrators. Meanwhile, the Vault depends on roles such as Curator, Guardian, and Owner; Oracle updates also involve DEFAULT ADMIN privileges. Even though the project uses a Timelock—meaning certain sensitive changes take 1 day to take effect—this still implies the risk users truly bear comes not only from the smart contracts, but also from who sets the parameters, who can change them, and who has the authority to handle things if something goes wrong.

And oddly, we’re now at the time when it’s easiest to just look at the hype. The official team has already set the TGE for August 25. The closer we get to token issuance, the more I want to focus on these “unsexy” aspects: Will administrator permissions be further delegated later on? Who exactly controls the Oracle and the Guardian? After extreme market conditions trigger physical delivery, who will bear the collateral discount and liquidity risk? #BTC #ETH 

I agree with the fixed-rate direction, but the word “fixed” can’t end up meaning only the number is fixed while users’ expectations about the risk boundary are not. I think this is something @TermMax needs to answer after the TGE.

#TermMax $TermMax @termmax

content:
这两天我把 @TermMax 的文档认真翻了一遍，我最大的感觉不是“固定利率终于有人做了”，而是另一个问题：TermMax 固定的到底只是利率，还是连风险也给用户一种“被固定住”的错觉？

TermMax 最吸引人的设计很直接：借款成本提前锁死，FT 到期按固定价值赎回。听着确实舒服，但往下看清算机制，事情就没这么简单了。官方文档自己写得很清楚，如果极端行情下清算没有完全执行，FT 持有人最后拿到的可能不只是原本借出的资产，而是按比例接收抵押物；而且抵押物价值甚至可能不足以完全覆盖本金和利息。

这就出现了我觉得最值得讨论的矛盾：收益率是固定的，底层信用和清算结果却不是固定的。

再往权限层看更有意思。一个 Market 里的抵押资产、到期日、LLTV、是否开启杠杆等核心参数，本身由 TermMax 管理员配置；Vault 又依赖 Curator、Guardian、Owner 等角色，Oracle 更新也存在 DEFAULT ADMIN 权限。虽然项目做了 Timelock，部分敏感修改默认要等 1 天，但这仍然意味着用户真正承担的风险，不只来自智能合约，还来自参数是谁定、谁能改、出问题时谁有权处理。

偏偏现在又到了最容易只看热度的时候——官方已经把 TGE 定在 8 月 25 日。 越接近发币，我反而越想看这些“不性感”的东西：管理员权限以后会不会进一步下放？Oracle 和 Guardian 到底由谁控制？极端行情触发实物交割后，谁来承担抵押物折价和流动性风险？#BTC #ETH 

固定利率这个方向我认可，但“固定”两个字不能最后只固定了数字，却没有固定用户对风险边界的预期。这个问题，我觉得 @TermMax 在 TGE 之后反而更需要回答。

title: China’s Economy Has a Bigger Problem Than One Bad Number — And Crypto Investors Should Pay Attention
subTitle:
China’s latest economic data is sending a message that investors should not ignore.
At first glance, this may look like another disappointing retail-sales report. But the bigger story is much broader.
China is now dealing with weak consumer demand, falling investment, slowing industrial activity and a property sector that continues to drag on household confidence.
That combination matters—not only for China, but potentially for global markets and risk assets, including crypto.
And this is where I think investors need to look beyond the headline numbers.
📉 China’s July Data Was Weak Across Multiple Areas
China’s July economic figures showed a noticeable loss of momentum.
Industrial production grew 4.5% year-on-year, slowing from 5.3% in June and missing the 4.8% market expectation.
Retail sales were even weaker.
Consumer spending increased only 0.6% year-on-year, down from 1% in June and significantly below the roughly 1.5% expectation.
But the number that caught my attention most was investment.
Fixed-asset investment declined 6.7% during the first seven months of 2026, compared with a 5.7% decline through June.
So this isn't simply a “bad retail-sales number.”
It is a broader slowdown in domestic economic momentum.
And that is much more important.
🏠 The Property Problem Is Still Sitting in the Background
China's property market remains one of the biggest obstacles to a stronger domestic recovery.
New-home prices in July were down around 3.2% from a year earlier, while household wealth remains heavily connected to real estate.
When property prices remain under pressure, consumers tend to become more cautious.
People delay buying homes.
They save more.
They reduce discretionary spending.
Businesses become more cautious about investment.
And that creates a difficult cycle:
Weak property market → weaker confidence → weaker consumption → weaker investment → slower growth.
Breaking that cycle is much harder than simply announcing another short-term stimulus package.
🇨🇳 Beijing Now Has a Bigger Job
China's policymakers have already been trying to support domestic demand, but the latest numbers suggest that the existing measures have not yet created a broad-based recovery.
Chinese officials have indicated that counter-cyclical policy adjustments will be strengthened, while Premier Li Qiang has also called for efforts to stabilize external demand and expand trade cooperation.
The key question now is:
Will Beijing become more aggressive with fiscal and economic support?
Because there is a major difference between supporting selected industries and actually putting money into the hands of consumers.
China can continue to support advanced manufacturing, technology and exports.
But if household spending and private investment remain weak, the recovery could remain uneven.
That is exactly what investors need to watch.
⚠️ Strong Exports Are Not Enough Forever
One interesting part of the current picture is that China's export sector has remained relatively resilient.
Global demand, particularly around technology and AI-related infrastructure, has helped Chinese factories maintain activity despite weaker domestic demand.
But relying heavily on exports creates another problem.
If China's domestic economy remains weak while exports continue to dominate growth, trade tensions with major economies could become even more important.
That means China faces a difficult balancing act:
Stimulate domestic demand without creating excessive leverage.
Support growth without reigniting property-sector risks.
Maintain exports while avoiding stronger trade restrictions from major partners.
This is why I don't think today's data should be viewed as a simple bearish headline.
It is a policy test.
🌍 Why Global Markets Should Care
China is one of the world's most important engines of global demand.
When Chinese consumers and companies spend less, the effects can spread through commodities, manufacturing, shipping, emerging markets and global risk sentiment.
But there is another side to this story.
If Beijing responds with stronger fiscal stimulus, additional consumer support, infrastructure spending or monetary easing, markets could quickly start pricing in a different economic environment.
That could create a sharp shift in sentiment.
Bad data can sometimes become bullish later—if it forces policymakers to act aggressively.
That's the part I will be watching.
₿ What Does This Mean for Crypto?
For crypto, the relationship isn't as simple as:
Weak China = Bitcoin down.
Bitcoin trades in a global liquidity environment.
What matters more is how policymakers respond and whether their response improves or damages overall risk appetite.
If China's weakness leads to stronger stimulus and broader global liquidity expectations, risk assets could eventually benefit.
On the other hand, if the weakness continues without a meaningful policy response, investors may prefer defensive positioning and volatility could remain elevated.
That creates both risk and opportunity for crypto traders.
But I would not chase the first move.
I would watch liquidity, market structure, dollar strength, bond yields and institutional flows before making aggressive decisions.
🟠 $BTC  — The Established Market Leader
For me, BTC remains the first name to watch when the global macro environment changes.
Bitcoin is the most established crypto asset and generally has deeper liquidity than the majority of the market.
If global liquidity expectations improve and risk appetite returns, BTC is likely to remain one of the primary beneficiaries within crypto.
But the opposite is also true.
If China weakness develops into a broader global risk-off event, Bitcoin can experience sharp volatility before any potential recovery.
So my approach would be simple:
Don't chase the headline. Watch the reaction.
If BTC absorbs negative macro news without breaking important market structure, that can be more meaningful than the economic headline itself.
🔵 $ETH  — Watching for Confirmation
ETH is another established asset I would keep on the radar.
Ethereum tends to attract attention when investors become more comfortable taking risk across the broader crypto market.
But ETH needs confirmation from the overall market.
I would rather see:
BTC stabilizing → market liquidity improving → ETH/BTC strengthening → broader altcoin participation.
That sequence would be much healthier than randomly buying altcoins simply because China released weak economic numbers.
For me, ETH remains a higher-beta established crypto asset worth watching if risk appetite starts returning.
🟡 $BNB  — A Different Type of Exposure
BNB also remains on my established-asset watchlist.
Its investment case is different from BTC and ETH because of its strong connection to the Binance ecosystem and broader exchange-related crypto activity.
That means BNB can benefit when trading activity and crypto participation expand—but it also remains sensitive to regulatory developments and the overall health of the crypto market.
So I would treat BNB as part of a diversified crypto watchlist rather than assuming macro weakness automatically makes it bullish.
🎯 The Bigger Investment Lesson
The biggest mistake investors can make right now is focusing on only one number.
Retail sales missed expectations.
But the real story is:
Consumption is weak.
Investment is weakening.
Industrial momentum is slowing.
Property remains under pressure.
And policymakers are facing increasing pressure to generate stronger domestic demand.
That creates two possible paths.
🟢 Scenario 1 — Beijing Acts Aggressively
If China introduces meaningful measures that successfully improve household confidence, consumption and investment, global risk sentiment could improve.
In that environment, crypto could eventually benefit through stronger risk appetite and improved liquidity expectations.
BTC would be my first asset to watch, followed by ETH and BNB.
🔴 Scenario 2 — Policy Response Remains Too Weak
If stimulus remains limited while property weakness and weak consumer confidence continue, China's slowdown could become more persistent.
That would increase uncertainty across global markets.
In that scenario, I would prioritize capital preservation and wait for stronger confirmation instead of blindly buying dips.
💡 My Take
I don't think China's July data is a reason to panic.
But I also don't think investors should ignore it.
The important question is no longer:
“Did China have a bad month?”
The better question is:
“What will Beijing do next?”
Because if policymakers respond aggressively, today's weak economic data could eventually become the foundation for a stronger liquidity-driven recovery.
If they don't, the market may continue to price in slower growth and higher uncertainty.
For crypto investors, that means patience becomes extremely important.
I'm keeping BTC, ETH and BNB on my established spot-market watchlist—but I would rather buy strength supported by improving liquidity and market structure than gamble on the first reaction to a macro headline.
Weak economic data creates volatility.
Policy response creates direction.
And right now, the policy response is the part I am watching most closely.
This is a market analysis, not financial advice. Crypto remains highly volatile, and investors should manage position size and risk accordingly.

#termmax @termmax  Many players who are just getting started with TermMax always wonder: if it claims to be a fixed interest rate, why do people get completely different rates from the same pool? This isn’t actually trying to fool anyone—what matters is exactly which second the “lock-in” action takes effect.

On this platform, “fixed” definitely isn’t a one-size-fits-all, whole-pool uniform price. Its real meaning is that the moment you click to confirm and your order is finalized, the lending cost of that money is irrevocably set. After that, even if the market’s capital utilization rate surges wildly, the interest you owe will not increase by even a penny.

If it can lock the cost, why is the quoted price different for everyone? That comes down to the range-based order-book design behind it. Large lenders don’t just offer a single rigid number. Instead, they distribute their funds across different APR tiers along a yield curve.

When borrowers enter the market, it’s essentially queuing to shop. The cheapest funds with the very low interest rate at the front of the line are always taken first. People who join later who still want to borrow will have to accept the next, higher price tier with no choice.

So the price you ultimately get depends entirely on how much inventory is left in the order book at the time, and how big your appetite is. If you borrow only a little, you might just happen to consume the cheapest available portion. But if your order is huge, it will definitely cut through multiple interest-rate ranges. Because you end up using more expensive funds from later tiers, the overall average cost of the entire sum naturally gets pushed higher. When the order book depth is insufficient, large capital entering the market will raise the barrier for itself.

What most easily trips up beginners is the operating interface. The page always only highlights that lowest, most eye-catching edge APR, but it doesn’t directly show the true weighted cost calculated based on your actual borrow amount. Many people therefore treat the “starting price” as the final unit price for buying all the available funds.

In short, TermMax’s mechanics are more like a segmented pricing schedule: the cheap额度 you just bought is exactly the price promised—no reneging. But if you want to borrow more, sorry—the next labels are priced higher to begin with.

content:
#termmax @termmax  不少玩家刚接触 TermMax 时总会纳闷：明明宣称是固定利息，怎么同一个池子里，大伙儿拿到的利率却千差万别？这其实并非协议在忽悠人，弄懂它的关键，得看这个“锁定”动作是从哪一秒开始生效的。

在这个平台上，“固定”绝对不是吃大锅饭式的全场统一定价。它的真实含义是，当你点下确认、单子敲定的那一瞬间，这笔钱的借贷代价就彻底拍板了。往后哪怕市场里的资金利用率狂飙突进，你要负担的利息也一分都不会多。

既然能锁死成本，为何对外要价还不一样？这要归功于它背后的区间挂单设计。提供资金的大户们不会只给出一个死板的数字，而是顺着一条收益曲线，把手头的钱分散布置在不同的 APR 档位里。

借钱的人进场，其实就是在排队扫货。排在最前面、利息极低的便宜资金总是最先被抢光。后面入场的人要想继续拿钱，就只能硬着头皮去接受下一档更贵的要价。

因此，你最终拿到什么价格，全看当时盘面还剩多少存货，以及你的胃口有多大。如果你只是小打小闹借一点，可能刚好消耗掉最便宜的那点份额。但如果你的单子极大，肯定会直接打穿好几个利率区间。由于动用了后面更贵的资金，整笔巨款的平均成本自然就被拉升了。当盘口深度不够时，大资金进场本身就会抬高自己的门槛。

现在最容易让新手吃亏的，就是操作界面。页面上永远只亮出那个最低、最吸睛的边缘 APR，却不直接显示按你实际借款额算出来的加权真实成本。很多人因此把“起步价”当成了买断全部资金的最终单价。

说白了，TermMax 的玩法更像是一张分段计费的价目表：你刚买下的那点便宜额度，说好多少钱就是多少钱，绝不赖账；但如果你还想再拿更多，对不起，接下来的标价本来就更贵。

#termmax @termmax  mentions TermMax, a fixed-rate lending platform. Many players often feel puzzled: since it’s all in the same liquidity pool, why do the interest rates everyone ultimately receives differ so widely? This is not a contract flaw; the key lies in how the interest-accruing effective node is defined. In its underlying logic, the real meaning of “fixed” is this: as long as the transaction is successfully executed, the borrowing cost is completely locked in. Even if the overall market’s capital utilization rate goes absolutely wild afterward, the repayment pressure for that liability will never rise in tandem.

If it can lock in costs, why does the outward pricing vary so dramatically? The answer is hidden in its unique range order (Range Order) mechanism. The market maker will never rigidly offer a single, immutable number. Instead, like laying out a trading grid, they distribute the chips they hold along an invisible yield curve, spreading them across different APR (annual percentage rate) tiers.

The behavior of borrowing users, in essence, is to consume the pool’s liquidity in sequence. The low-interest chips at the very front are always used up first. If later entrants want to keep borrowing, they have no choice but to accept a higher asking price.

This perfectly explains the price discrepancies caused by the size of the capital pool. Retail demand is small, so the small cheap额度 at the front can satisfy it; when large capital enters, it can power through and pierce multiple interest-rate ranges. Once you sum the capital across all tiers and compute the weighted average price, the overall average naturally gets pulled higher. This is the “slippage” in decentralized lending: when the order book depth is insufficient to absorb a massive buy, the very act of a large holder entering the market pushes up their own financial cost.

What most easily causes newcomers to suffer is actually the display strategy on the front-end page. The interface always shows that most tempting marginal best APR, but it deliberately hides the weighted costs that would be recalculated based on the actual input amount. Many people see the starting price and assume—incorrectly—that it’s the final average price for the whole round. In plain terms, TermMax is like a stepped-quote invoice: the interest on the portion of chips you buy is guaranteed not to be reneged on; but if you want to keep sweeping downward for more, the next tier’s price will inevitably be more expensive.

既然能锁死成本，为何对外报价又千姿百态？答案藏在其独特的区间挂单（Range Order）玩法中。这里的做市商绝不会死板地给出一个僵化的单一数字，而是像铺设交易网格那样，将手里的筹码沿着一条隐形的收益曲线，分摊摆放到不同的 APR（年化收益率）档位上。

借款用户的行为，本质上是在按顺序“啃食”池子里的流动性。排在最前方的低息筹码总是最先被消耗殆尽，后入场者若想继续拿钱，只能退而求其次去接受更高的要价。

这完美解释了资金规模造成的价格落差。散户需求小，前端的那点便宜额度就能满足；大资金进场则会势如破竹般击穿数个利率区间。将各档位的资金加总核算，综合均价自然被拉高。这就是去中心化借贷领域的“滑点”：当盘口深度不足以承接巨量买单时，大户的入场动作本身，就在推升自身的财务代价。

目前最容易让新手吃亏的，其实是前端页面的展示套路。界面永远挂着那个最诱人的边际最优 APR，却故意隐去了按实际输入规模重新计算的加权开销。很多人看到起步价，就想当然地以为那是包揽全场的最终均价。说白了，TermMax 就像一份阶梯报价账单：你买定的那段筹码，约定好的利息绝不耍赖；但若想接着往下扫货，下一档的标价必然更加昂贵。

#termmax @termmax  After a deep dive into TermMax’s Range Order AMM, the biggest takeaway is this: on-chain lending has finally broken out of the old ways of thinking. Previously, when using Aave to deposit or withdraw, whether interest is high or low depended entirely on how congested the liquidity pool was—effectively the system forcibly draws a utilization-rate curve, and players can only passively pay the price. But TermMax went big: it directly abstracts “interest” into an asset-like target that can be freely bought and sold on the order book.

Now, market makers can shape their expected profit curve however they like; underneath, the system maintains balance through $vX_t \times vF_t = L^2$. The resulting immediate annualized return rate is $(vF_t/vX_t) \times (365/\text{remaining days})$. Put simply, the liquidity provider can operate the way you would place limit orders on a centralized exchange: for the first 500,000 U of额度, I only charge a 15% return; but if the borrowing size reaches 3,000,000 U, then sorry—the interest rate has to jump to 23%.

To make this aggressive route truly work in practice, it hinges on two extremely clever design choices:

“Black-or-white” binary matching: When taking an order into the book, the fill comes with a built-in slippage red line; if it exceeds the threshold, the entire order is automatically voided. This completely leaves behind the chain of traps in traditional decentralized liquidity pools—where the more you eat the order, the worse the slippage gets.

Cross-segment smooth stitching: Supported by the formula $L'^2 = L^2 \times [(x'+\beta')^2/(x'+\beta)^2]$, the system can weld all those scattered报价 segments from different fund providers into a single continuous “interest-rate order table” with no gaps.

Old-school finance evolved over hundreds of years—from central bank guidance rates, to interbank lending quotes, and then all the way to SOFR that fully reflects market sentiment. Now, smart contracts are rapidly replicating this process. As a pioneer who pushes the “order-book mechanism” to the extreme, the perspective for assessing TermMax’s potential must change: the TVL on the books has long lost its reference value. What truly tests the metal is the actual thickness of the buy/sell books that Curators painstakingly place.

However, this pure matching model has a fatal weakness—extreme reliance on cold start. If the order book lacks “mindless” retail liquidity that routinely provides the base, then the moment professional institutions stop participating, the entire system will grind to a halt. What the official side has released so far—Atomic Orders, and moving idle ammunition into Aave to earn yield—is, frankly speaking, essentially the project team subsidizing from its own pocket. $ETH #eth

In the past, everyone was used to the Aave-style playbook: the protocol draws a line based on the capital utilization rate, and users can only passively accept it. But TermMax turns the “lending interest rate” into a tradable asset. Market makers can lay out their own segmented yield curve. Inside the pool, it strictly follows the constant product rule $vX_t \times vF_t = L^2$. The real-time APR is essentially a direct mapping from the virtual reserve ratio: $(vF_t/vX_t) \times (365/\text{remaining days})$. Put simply, lenders can now place limit orders like trading crypto: with the top 500k U, I only want 15% interest; but if your borrowing size reaches 3 million U, then the rate has to be pulled up to 23%.

This logic works thanks to two hardcore design choices. First is a “black-or-white” binary matching mechanism: when a borrower comes to take the order, they include a slippage floor; if the match can’t be found, the entire order is canceled outright. It never suffers the slippage losses that come from continuously hammering a traditional liquidity pool. Second, to align all kinds of capital quotes across different segments, the system introduces a cross-segment smoothing formula: $L'^2 = L^2 \times [(x'+\beta')^2/(x'+\beta)^2]$. With this algorithm as backup, fragmented limit orders are seamlessly stitched into a continuous “interest-rate order book.”

DeFi is using code to accelerate like crazy, retracing the same old paths that traditional finance has followed for hundreds of years—moving from one-size-fits-all benchmark guidance prices, to institutional quotes, and then toward full-on market competition. As a pure quote-driven testbed, the standard for measuring TermMax’s strength has long changed. The TVL sitting in the pool is just artificially fat; it’s the actual order-book depth that Curators truly report that really is its moat.

However, a deadlock of this pure matching approach is the difficulty of cold start. The system doesn’t have passive LPs who only want stable returns to act as “blood bags.” Once professional players stop, the order book instantly turns into a ghost town. The official push right now—Atomic Orders, and also parking idle capital in Aave to earn extra yield—is, in plain terms, about spending money to buy habits, and using subsidies to artificially sustain early liquidity. #termmax @termmax  盘了一下 TermMax 的 Range Order AMM，底层机制确实让人眼界大开。过去大家习惯了 Aave 那套玩法，协议按资金使用率画一条线，用户只能被动接受。但 TermMax 直接把“借贷利率”做成了能交易的标的。做市商可以自己铺设分段收益曲线，池内严格遵循 $vX_t \times vF_t = L^2$ 的恒定乘积，实时的 APR 其实就是虚拟储备比的直接映射：$(vF_t/vX_t) \times (365/\text{剩余天数})$。说得通俗点，资金方现在能像炒币一样挂限价单：头部的 50万 U 资金我只要 15% 的利息，但如果你的借款规模吃到 300万 U，那利率就得拉到 23%。

这套逻辑能跑通，全靠两个硬核设定支撑。首先是“非黑即白”的二元撮合：借款人来吃单时自带滑点底线，要是匹配不上直接整笔撤销，绝不吃传统资金池那种连续砸盘的滑点亏。其次，为了让各路资金五花八门的报价能对齐，系统引入了跨段平滑公式：$L'^2 = L^2 \times [(x'+\beta')^2/(x'+\beta)^2]$。有这个算法托底，碎片化的挂单就被无缝缝合成了一本连续的“利率订单簿”。

DeFi 正在用代码疯狂加速，重走传统金融几百年的老路——从一刀切的基准指导价，过渡到机构报价，再走向完全的市场博弈。作为纯报价制的试验田，衡量 TermMax 实力的标准早就变了。躺在池子里的 TVL 都是虚胖，所有 Curator 实打实报出来的盘口厚度，才是它真正的护城河。

不过，这种纯撮合玩法的死穴在于冷启动太难。系统里没有那些只图安稳的被动 LP 充当“血包”，一旦专业玩家停手，订单簿立马变成鬼城。官方现在力推的 Atomic Orders，还有把闲置资金丢给 Aave 赚外快，说穿了都是在花钱买习惯，用补贴强行维系早期的流动性。这套机制能不能活下来，全看能不能熬过这段无人问津的真空期。总之，以后研究 TermMax，别再扯 TVL，直接去盯它的利率盘口有多深。#eth $ETH

The US has officially passed stablecoin legislation: this time they don’t just support it in words—it’s written into federal law

The GENIUS Act officially takes effect, and the US is establishing a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins—directly bullish for BTC and ETH.

The US has officially legislated the GENIUS Act. This is the first nationwide stablecoin regulatory framework in the United States. In plain terms: issuing stablecoins will require full reserves, audits, and a federal license. Until now, this industry has been in a gray area—institutions wanted to enter the market but were afraid of stepping over regulatory red lines. Now the rules are clear.

One-sentence translation: Before, there were no rules so people didn’t dare to play; now, the rules are written, and big money can enter legitimately.

Market impact
- Short term: Regulatory clarity → institutions and traditional financial institutions dare to allocate to stablecoin assets → on-chain liquidity pools expand → stablecoins become the “entry ticket” to the crypto market, with incremental capital flowing into BTC and ETH. The current reactions of BTC at $63,524 and ETH at $1,897 are still relatively mild (24h gains are under 1%), suggesting the good news hasn’t been fully priced in yet.
- Medium term: Payment giants and banks will accelerate issuing their own stablecoins; the market share of compliant stablecoins will rise. The entire industry will shift from a “trading/speculation narrative” to “payment infrastructure,” and valuation logic will follow suit.

My take
Clearly bullish. Regulatory implementation is the most certain type of positive catalyst in this cycle because it’s irreversible—after the law takes effect, it won’t be repealed just because the market turns bearish. BTC is ranging around $63,524. If it breaks above the $65,000 area on increased volume within 12 hours, the trend is confirmed. Conversely, if it falls back below $62,000, it suggests that macro liquidity is still putting pressure on prices, and the regulatory tailwind will need more time to be digested. ETH typically has greater elasticity; at $1,897, it’s only about 5% away from the $2,000 psychological level—worth watching.

Key risks: The execution timeline of the law’s details may be slower than expected. Don’t treat long-term positives as a short-term catalyst.

GENIUS法案正式生效，美国给稳定币立了联邦监管框架，直接利多BTC和ETH。

美国把GENIUS法案正式立法了，这是美国第一套全国性的稳定币监管框架。说白了，以后发稳定币要有全额储备、要接受审计、要拿到联邦牌照。之前这个行业一直处在灰色地带，机构想进场但怕踩监管红线，现在规则明确了。

一句话翻译：以前是没规则不敢玩，现在是规则写好了，大钱可以名正言顺进来了。

对市场的影响
- 短期：监管明确→机构和传统金融机构敢于配置稳定币资产→链上资金池扩容→稳定币是加密市场的“入场券”，增量资金通过稳定币进入BTC、ETH。目前BTC $63,524、ETH $1,897的反应还比较温和（24h涨幅不到1%），说明利好没被完全定价。
- 中期：支付巨头和银行会加速发自己的稳定币，合规稳定币市占率提升，整个行业从“炒作叙事”转向“支付基础设施”，估值逻辑会跟着变。

我的判断
明确看多。监管落地是本轮周期里确定性最高的一类利好，因为它不可逆——法律生效后不会因为行情差就撤销。BTC在$63,524附近横盘，如果12小时内放量突破$65,000一线，趋势确认；反之若跌回$62,000下方，说明宏观资金面还在压制，监管利好需要更长时间消化。ETH弹性通常更大，$1,897的位置距离$2,000心理关口只有5%空间，值得关注。风险点：法案细节执行节奏可能低于预期，别把长期利好当成短期催化剂。

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  In regular vulnerability battles, what most often makes people’s hearts race is the moment when the authorities just announce that the “alert has been lifted.” Most retail investors, upon seeing the fix is complete, immediately assume all is well. Take the AEGIS patch for $DUSK  this time: the project team wiped out 39 vulnerabilities in one go (7 of them are classified as high-risk). At first glance, it’s reassuring. But after I dug into the Phoenix anonymous fee documentation, my brow tightened again.

The old billing logic really has a “everyone fights for themselves” kind of feel. For a transfer that involves privacy attributes, the original process was: first, declare in the credential “I’ll pay no more than this much in fees,” then settle based on actual consumption when it runs, and finally refund the remaining difference. The problem is that these three steps were not locked into a closed, self-contained framework.

That leaves room for insiders to exploit: tamper with execution data or swap out the receiving wallet. In severe cases, the system can even fabricate $DUSK out of thin air, directly undermining the token’s deflationary logic and its pricing/valuation framework; in even more extreme scenarios, causing parameter overflow can make nodes across the entire network grind to a halt—ultimately taking the whole chain down.

Now AEGIS has indeed gotten smarter: it has added two layers of reconciliation locks, and even the destination of the refunded coins is directly bound to the signing stage. The visible loopholes have been effectively shut. But the official, of course, had to add one extra reminder: cutting off the pathway for wrongdoing is completely different from digging out the underlying disease.

Once that line was said, my sense of crisis flared up again. In decentralized finance, the biggest fear is that the same pot of funds ends up with multiple ledgers across different stages. The current remediation is, at best, “treating headaches by curing headaches.” If the underlying code doesn’t coordinate into a single unified standard, then future iterations that add new features will sooner or later crash.

Regarding this trust crisis, I insist on a “staged settlement” style resolution logic: right now, plug the gaps, stem the bleeding for the moment, and call it passing the first checkpoint at best. It must wait for the underlying architecture to be rebuilt, plus a top-tier third-party institution to step in for a review, before deeper doubts can be fully dispelled. Only after the mainnet runs safely and steadily for a long stretch—without any relapse of old issues—can this account be considered truly closed. Whether the foundation is solid or not, I will keep treating it as the core yardstick for assessing @Dusk_Foundation ’s long-term investment value. #eth $ETH

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  平时做漏洞博弈的时候，最让人心惊肉跳的往往是官方刚刚宣布“警报解除”的那一刻。大部分散户看到修复完成，立马就以为万事大吉了。就拿这次 $DUSK 的 AEGIS 补丁来说，项目方一口气清除了 39 个隐患（其中有 7 个属于高危级别）。乍一看挺让人踏实，但我仔细扒了扒 Phoenix 匿名费用的说明，眉头又皱了起来。

老架构里的收费逻辑，确实有点“各自为战”的意思。一笔带隐私属性的转账，原本的流程是：先在凭证里声明“我顶多掏多少手续费”，实际跑起来再按消耗结算，最后把剩下的差额退回去。毛病就出在，这三步操作没被锁死在一个封闭框架内。

这就给了懂行的人可乘之机：随意篡改执行数据或是换掉收款钱包。严重的话，系统甚至会无中生有地多印出 $DUSK，直接冲击代币的通缩逻辑与价格估值体系；再极端些，把参数搞溢出，能让全网节点一起罢工，导致整条链彻底瘫痪。

现在 AEGIS 确实学聪明了，上了两道对账锁，退币去向也直接绑定在签名环节。明面上的缺口算是掐断了。可官方偏偏多嘴提醒了一句：掐断作恶路径，和挖掉底层病灶，完全是两项工程。

这话一出，我的危机感立马又上来了。搞去中心化金融，最怕的就是同一笔资金，在不同环节出现好几个账本。现在的补救充其量是“头痛医头”，如果底层代码不统筹归位唯一标准，将来迭代新功能迟早还得翻车。

对于这次信任危机，我坚持“分期付款”式的解除逻辑：眼下堵住破绽，暂时止血，顶多算过了第一关。必须等底层架构重塑，外加第三方顶级机构介入复核，这才能打消更深层的疑虑。必须等主网安安稳稳跑上一大段时间，没有任何旧病复发，这笔账才算彻底翻篇。底层根基究竟扎不扎实，我会一直把它当做衡量 @Dusk_Foundation 长期投资价值的核心准绳。#eth $ETH

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation  Occasionally, I catch trading opportunities brought about by security incidents. To be honest, the moment the project team just released the patch notice is actually the ultimate test of judgment. The market is so easily lulled by the words “resolved,” assuming the alert is completely gone. This AEGIS upgrade released by $DUSK  cleared 39 vulnerabilities in one go (including 7 critical ones). It certainly sounds reassuring on the surface, but when I skimmed the details of Phoenix’s privacy fee adjustments, I couldn’t help but feel we shouldn’t be complacent.

In the old mechanism, the different steps were badly disconnected. With an anonymous transfer, it first reports a fee upper limit in the “proof,” then during “execution” it calculates the real gas cost, and finally refunds the remaining balance back to the account. What’s deadly is that these three steps weren’t tightly bound by the same set of rules. Hackers can take advantage by tampering with execution data or the payee. On the smaller end, they could intercept someone else’s refund; on the bigger end, the system might somehow “spit out” extra $DUSK out of thin air—effectively a backdoor form of money printing. They could even intentionally trigger parameter explosions, causing all nodes to error out together and directly bring the network down.

Now AEGIS has indeed made targeted fixes. It not only added two reconciliation checkpoints, but also embedded the refund address into the signature—closing off all the obvious malicious paths. But what gives me pause is the official supplementary statement: stopping the routes used for wrongdoing and digging out the underlying root causes are two entirely different things. Right now, with the漏洞 (vulnerabilities) sealed, the down payment has been handled. Only after the underlying rewrite is truly completed and the project obtains an independent audit report can the second phase land. In the end, it still depends on real-world testing: as long as the mainnet runs for a long time without incident, the final payment can be considered settled.

As long as the vulnerabilities involve token over-issuance, downtime, or fund security, the main capital will absolutely keep its distance. Naturally, on-chain gas consumption will also weaken accordingly. The proactive approach of hunting down issues is commendable, but just the word “fix” isn’t enough for me to be fully at ease. 基于此，我认为市场对DUSK的安全折价只能像按揭一样“分期”消化。眼下漏洞封堵，算结了首付；等底层真正重写完毕并拿到独立机构的审计报告，才算二期落地；最后还得靠真实环境检验，主网长期不出岔子，尾款才算两清。

只要隐患牵扯到代币超发、宕机或资金安全，主力资金绝对会保持距离，链上的 Gas 消耗自然也会跟着疲软。这次主动排雷的态度值得肯定，但仅凭“修复”两字还不足以让我彻底放心，底层架构的稳固度，依然是我研判 @Dusk_Foundation 长期估值的核心标尺。#eth $ETH

It’s like the fat I cut last week—this morning I weighed myself again and it came back. The Fear & Greed Index is 50, neither high nor low, stuck in the middle. The market’s mood is even more muted than my love life; both long and short sides are testing each other on their screens, and nobody dares to make the first move.

ETH is actually a bit more interesting: 1,907.56, +1.2% over 24 hours, and +1.6% over 7 days. Among mainstream coins it’s like a top student. The funding rate is 0.0072%, as normal as it can get—meaning leveraged funds aren’t doing anything reckless. I think ETH may keep grinding within the 1,880–1,930 range in the near term. If you’re bullish, watch for a pullback around 1,880; stop-loss below 1,850, and take-profit first target at 1,950. Don’t ask me why I’m being so conservative—ask the market, I’ve been educated by it too many times. Now I know how to respect it.

The gainers list today is basically a magic show. GPS is directly up +60.91%—at a price of 0.0162, with 550 million USDT in 24-hour turnover. That volume is stronger than many mainstream coins. To be honest, I didn’t expect this thing to fly that high. But the Web3 security track story really can be told. Still, the risk-reward of chasing that rally isn’t very attractive—just watch the show. TUT is up +41.34%: a tutorial coin made by a developer who taught others to issue tokens on the BNB Chain 10 months ago. This script, if placed into a novel, would definitely get sent back by an editor to be rewritten. But the market just buys it. STAR is also up +31.98% and hit the hot search. Yet the funding rate is 0.1124%, which already signals that longs may be getting overheated. Chasing at this point feels no different from running in an oil-heating summer day wearing a down jacket—sweating is minor; heatstroke is the real issue.

On the losers list, VELVET is -42.73%, and CYS is -38.11%. Both funding rates show shorts are overheated. After this kind of sharp drop, negative funding rates sometimes create a chance for an oversold rebound trade. But honestly, catching these falling knives can easily end up cutting your hand. Better to be honest and stick with the mainstream. BEAT is also down -25.27% on the losers list. It might have been in a group chat yesterday shouting “BEAT to the moon,” but now it’s back on Earth.

On the hot search list, both XRP and HYPE are there—but my attention is on Pump.fun. This platform is basically a meme coin assembly line factory. Every time it hits the hot search, it means market sentiment is shifting toward speculation. At times like this, I remind myself: don’t let FOMO get you in the head. Position management matters more than anything.

Let’s summarize today’s trading ideas: BTC and ETH are more stable—good for swing trades. Among the altcoins, GPS and TUT are the ones that pump violently—just look at the commotion. STAR needs extra caution for an overheat pullback. For anything with abnormal funding rates, observe first—don’t rush to bottom-fish.

Remember: staying alive matters more than making more money. Because the market has opportunities every day—once your principal is gone, it’s really gone.

Finally, I’ll ask the brothers one question: do you think this altcoin season is truly here, or is it just another round of “the wolf is coming”? Drop your thoughts in the comments—I’ll be squatting here watching. Anyway, it’s 2 a.m., and I can’t sleep.

Brothers, ETH is around 1908 right now. After nearly a week of consolidating in the box from 1860 to 1900, it has finally pushed up to the upper boundary—only the last little push away from the 24-hour high of 1915.

First, the conclusion—news is blowing hot, but the money hasn’t followed. I won’t chase at this level; I’ll wait for it to choose its direction on its own.

What stands out most is sentiment. In the 24-hour news cycle, the “bull” voices are pressing down on the “bear” ones—institutions stacking coins, ETF inflows returning, banks’ app integrations moving on-chain, upgrade proposals, and story after story that sounds solid. On top of that, the mining side bought another nearly ten thousand coins in one go. Sentiment scores are almost maxed out.

But when you look at the data, it gives itself away. The technical indicators still show a dead cross on the MACD, price is trading below the 10-day line, and the volume hasn’t even reached half of the average volume—this rally has no volume confirmation. In the spot market, within a three-hour window, large orders saw net outflows of over ten thousand coins. Whale accounts also quietly trimmed longs, while retail accounts have about 70% still holding longs. Meanwhile, leverage borrowing has jumped more than sixty-fold compared to the last 12 hours.

In plain terms, right now the story is strong, the technicals are weak, the smart money is reducing, and leverage is increasing. The funding rate is still lying low on the floor and hasn’t heated up. This doesn’t look like a forced squeeze—more like news hype has pushed the price up to the upper boundary.

This directly affects two key parties: first, U.S. domestic issuers (like Circle) gain a relative advantage; second, compliance costs for offshoring issuers will rise significantly.

This news is essentially another step toward regulatory implementation, and the direction is neutral. When DeFi starts taking “maturity” seriously, what problem is TermMax trying to solve?
Why does DeFi always chase higher APYs, yet rarely think seriously about whether “interest rates can be determined”? After researching @termmax , I believe what it truly aims to fill is not yet another lending entry point, but the missing term structure for long-term finance on-chain.
Traditional floating-rate lending has a very practical problem: when the market gets crowded, the cost of capital changes rapidly. A strategy that looks good today may have its profit margins eaten up just days later if the borrowing rate suddenly rises. For ordinary users, this means returns are hard to predict; for institutions that need to allocate capital long term, it means both budgets and risk exposure are difficult to manage.#ETH  
TermMax’s approach is to make each market clearly specify, from the start, the debt asset, the collateral asset, and the maturity date—then split different rights via FT, XT, and GT. FT can be understood as zero-coupon bond–like instruments: purchased at a discount, redeemed at face value at maturity, so the yield can be calculated up front. XT captures another portion of value related to interest and strategy, while GT records the collateral and debt positions. What used to be tangled together in a single loan—maturity, yield, and risk—is separated into a structure that can be identified and priced on-chain.
What I find most worth关注 here is not a temporarily higher APY on some page, but “certainty” itself becoming a tradable product. Fixed borrowing costs help strategy users lock in costs, and fixed maturity-linked returns make it easier for capital providers to plan their schedules. If on-chain capital continues to grow in the future, what the market will need won’t be just liquidity—it will also need a truly usable yield curve.#BTC  
Of course, fixed rates don’t mean there is no risk. Collateral price volatility, liquidation thresholds, market depth, contract security, and liquidity before maturity all still need to be assessed separately. TermMax addresses interest-rate uncertainty, but it does not eliminate all risks for users.
So my first impression of TermMax is this: it’s not simply moving traditional bonds onto the chain—it’s trying to build “a price for time” for DeFi. It may not be flashy, but it could be an essential piece of infrastructure that on-chain finance must add as it matures.#termmax  @termmax

content:
当DeFi开始认真讨论“期限”，TermMax在解决什么问题？
为什么DeFi总在追逐更高的APY，却很少认真讨论“利率能不能确定”？研究 @termmax  之后，我觉得它真正想补上的，不是又一个借贷入口，而是链上金融长期缺失的期限结构。
传统浮动利率借贷有一个很现实的问题：市场一拥挤，资金成本就会迅速变化。今天看起来不错的策略，可能因为借款利率突然上升，几天后利润空间就被吃掉。对普通用户来说，这意味着收益难以预估；对需要长期配置资金的机构来说，则意味着预算和风险敞口都很难管理。#ETH  
TermMax的思路，是让每个市场从一开始就明确债务资产、抵押资产和到期日，再通过FT、XT与GT把不同权利拆开。FT可以理解为零息债券式凭证：以折价获得，到期按面值赎回，因此收益在进入时就能计算。XT承接与利息和策略相关的另一部分价值，而GT负责记录抵押品与债务仓位。原本混在一笔借贷里的期限、收益和风险，被拆成了可以在链上识别和定价的结构。
我认为这里最值得关注的，并不是某个页面上暂时更高的APY，而是“确定性”本身开始成为可交易的产品。固定借款成本能帮助策略使用者锁定成本，固定到期收益则让资金提供者更容易做期限安排。如果未来链上资金规模继续扩大，市场需要的不会只有流动性，还会需要一条真正可用的利率曲线。#BTC  
当然，固定利率不等于没有风险。抵押资产波动、清算阈值、市场深度、合约安全和到期前的流动性都需要单独评估。TermMax解决的是利率的不确定性，并没有替用户消除所有风险。
所以我对TermMax的第一印象是：它不是单纯把传统债券搬到链上，而是在尝试为DeFi建立“时间的价格”。这件事不够喧闹，却可能是链上金融走向成熟必须补的一块基础设施。#termmax  @termmax

Fixed interest rates—DeFi’s “coming-of-age” ritual?
In the past, when I looked into DeFi lending and borrowing, I was most easily drawn in by the APY shown on the homepage. But after using it for a while, I realized that the level of returns is only the surface. What really matters is whether you can calculate the costs upfront—because that determines whether a strategy can be executed consistently over the long term.

Floating interest rates are good for chasing real-time supply and demand, but they come with a built-in problem: when liquidity suddenly floods in or withdraws, borrowing costs move with it. A looped lending strategy, an interest-rate arbitrage (carry) setup, or a leveraged position that was originally calculated correctly may not be wrong because you misread the direction—it may be because the interest rate slipped out of control first. What TermMax aims to solve is this uncertainty: locking both the borrowing interest rate and the maturity date, so that on-chain capital can, for the first time, resemble a “bond” with cash flows you can plan. #BTC  

The most worth studying part isn’t the word “fixed” itself, but how three kinds of instruments—FT, XT, and GT—work together. FT is like a zero-coupon bond: you buy it at a discount, and at maturity you redeem it at face value. The yield is already locked in when you buy. XT is the complementary part of FT—at any moment, it satisfies 1 FT + 1 XT = 1 unit of debt asset. GT then uses an NFT to record the collateral and the debt, packaging leveraged positions into an identifiable on-chain credential. TermMax sets prices through an interest-rate-range AMM instead of forcing users to repeatedly perform manual looped borrowing. 

To me, the significance of this design isn’t to create more complex tokens, but to disentangle three things clearly: who provides the principal, who bears the time horizon, and who manages the collateral. If DeFi wants to serve DAO treasuries, market-making capital, and real-world mid- to long-term strategies, “high yield that changes at any time” simply isn’t enough. Predictable funding costs are the starting point for institutional-grade management. #ETH  

Of course, fixed interest rates don’t automatically mean fixed safety. You still need to check, item by item: liquidity before maturity, collateral volatility, liquidation thresholds, smart contract risk, and the depth of market making. Especially, the “maturity redemption logic” of FT and the time value embedded in XT shouldn’t be mistaken for risk-free yield.

So I’m paying attention to TermMax not because it promises higher returns, but because it answers a harder question: once market noise disappears, can on-chain capital have a yield curve that’s truly usable? If the answer holds, fixed interest rates may not just be a small niche in DeFi—it could be the foundation for DeFi’s move toward maturity. #termmax  @termmax

固定利率，才是 DeFi 的“成年礼”？
我过去看 DeFi 借贷，最容易被首页 APY 吸引。但真正用过一段时间后才发现，收益高低只是表面，能不能提前算清成本，才决定一套策略能否长期执行。

浮动利率适合追逐即时供需，却有一个天然问题：当资金突然涌入或撤出，借款成本会跟着变化。原本算好的循环贷、套息或杠杆仓位，可能不是方向看错了，而是利率先失控了。TermMax 想解决的，正是这份不确定性——把借款利率和到期日同时锁定，让链上资金第一次更像一张可以规划现金流的“债券”。#BTC  

它最值得研究的不是“固定”两个字，而是 FT、XT、GT 三种凭证如何协作。FT 类似零息债券：以折价买入，到期按面值赎回，买入时收益已经被锁定；XT 是 FT 的互补部分，任意时点满足 1 FT + 1 XT = 1 单位债务资产；GT 则以 NFT 记录抵押物与债务，把杠杆头寸装进一张可识别的链上凭证。TermMax 再通过面向利率区间的 AMM 进行定价，而不是让用户反复手动循环借贷。

这套设计的意义，在我看来不是制造更复杂的代币，而是把三件事拆清楚：谁提供本金、谁承担期限、谁管理抵押。DeFi 若想服务 DAO 金库、做市资金和真实的中长期策略，仅有“随时变化的高收益”远远不够；可预测的资金成本，才是机构化管理的起点。#ETH  

当然，固定利率不等于固定安全。到期前的流动性、抵押品波动、清算阈值、智能合约和做市深度仍要逐项检查。尤其 FT 的“到期兑付逻辑”和 XT 的时间价值，不该被简单理解成无风险收益。

所以我关注 TermMax，并不是因为它承诺了更高回报，而是它在回答一个更难的问题：当市场噪音消失后，链上资金能否拥有一条真正可使用的收益率曲线？如果答案成立，固定利率可能不是 DeFi 的一个小赛道，而是它走向成熟的基础设施。
#termmax  @termmax

When many people first come into contact with DeFi lending, their attention is often focused on how high the APY is, but they rarely ask: How long can this interest rate last?
Floating interest rates may seem flexible, but once capital utilization rises rapidly, borrowing costs will change along with it. The arbitrage or leverage strategies originally calculated may have the correct direction, yet the continually increasing interest will slowly eat away the profits. For those who truly manage capital, “not knowing how much interest you’ll have to pay next month” is itself a risk.#ETH 
That’s also why I started paying attention to TermMax. It doesn’t keep competing with higher numbers in floating-rate pools; instead, it tries to turn fixed terms and fixed interest rates into an on-chain tradable market.
One of TermMax’s key components is FT. You can think of it as an on-chain zero-coupon bond: lenders buy FT at a discount, and at maturity exchange it for the underlying assets at face value. The difference between the purchase price and the face value is the yield that has been locked in ahead of time. Borrowers, meanwhile, can determine their cost when opening a position, without having to guess day by day whether the pool’s interest rate might suddenly change. FT can also be traded in the market, so when conditions are favorable, borrowers can buy back FT to repay their debts.
In my view, what TermMax truly wants to do isn’t another “high-yield mining pool,” but to add to DeFi a missing piece of long-term interest rate infrastructure. Many traditional finance products are built on the premise that terms and interest rates can be priced. If on-chain finance relies only on floating rates that move with supply and demand, it’s hard to support longer-term, more complex capital needs.#BTC 
Of course, fixed interest rates don’t mean zero risk. You still need to assess collateral price, liquidation thresholds, contract security, and liquidity one by one. But pricing future uncertain costs upfront is valuable in its own right.
I’ll keep watching whether TermMax can build sufficiently deep liquidity. Because the real moat isn’t just a pretty model—it’s always having people willing to borrow, people willing to lend, and people willing to pay for certainty.#termmax  @termmax

很多人第一次接触 DeFi 借贷，注意力往往都放在 APY 有多高，却很少追问：这个利率能维持多久？
浮动利率看起来灵活，但资金利用率一旦快速上升，借款成本也会跟着变化。原本测算好的套利或杠杆策略，可能方向没有看错，利润却被不断抬升的利息慢慢吃掉。对真正管理资金的人来说，“不知道下个月要付多少利息”，本身就是一种风险。#ETH 
这也是我开始关注 TermMax 的原因。它没有继续在浮动利率池里卷更高的数字，而是尝试把固定期限、固定利率做成链上可交易的市场。
TermMax 的核心之一是 FT。可以把它理解成一种链上零息债券：出借人折价买入 FT，到期按面值兑换对应资产，买入价与面值之间的差额，就是提前锁定的收益；借款人则能在建立仓位时确定成本，不必每天猜测资金池利率会不会突然变化。FT 也可以在市场中交易，借款人可以在条件合适时买回 FT 偿还债务。
在我看来，TermMax 真正想做的并非另一个“高收益矿池”，而是给 DeFi 补上一块长期缺失的利率基础设施。传统金融的大量产品，都建立在期限和利率可以定价的前提上；链上金融如果只依赖随供需跳动的浮动利率，很难承载更长期、更复杂的资金需求。#BTC 
当然，固定利率不等于没有风险，抵押品价格、清算线、合约安全和流动性依然要逐项评估。但把未来的不确定成本提前标价，本身就很有价值。
我会继续观察 TermMax 能否做出足够深的流动性。因为真正的护城河，不只是模型漂亮，而是始终有人愿意借、有人愿意贷，也有人愿意为确定性付费。#termmax  @termmax

Tonight after washing up, I casually switched back and forth between the quote pages for several TermMax V2 terms more than a dozen times. The most direct feeling isn’t “the interest rate is really a steal,” but that it’s the same USDC—change the maturity date, and the price is like a market stall packing up: the farther you look, the less you can just focus on APY. Right now, the TermMax x Binance Booster prize pool has 1.7 million TMX, so the hype will pick up, but I’m still going to first look at how loans get settled. The most crucial blade in the whitepaper is splitting a single term debt into FT, XT, and GT: FT is the ERC-20 receivable that redeems at face value at maturity; XT carries the present value of the interest obligation. Together, the sum of their present values corresponds to one underlying debt asset. The borrower’s collateral and the debt owed are put into ERC-721 as GT, and changes in position size will synchronously alter the health factor. In this way, interest rates aren’t decided by the backend guessing—they’re the result of trades along a pricing curve from range orders, with maturity, price, and quantity all recorded on-chain. More interesting is the liquidation tail: if there’s extreme volatility or liquidity is too thin, and liquidation doesn’t recover enough underlying debt assets, the protocol will move to physical settlement. FT holders then take, proportionally from the pool, the underlying assets and collateral. It can’t make bad debt disappear, but it turns the illusion of “someone covering the losses” into a verifiable loss allocation. I’ll keep an eye on three things: curve depth, the GT liquidation threshold, and exiting liquidity before maturity. Fixed interest rates only fix the cost—they don’t fix the token price, and they don’t fix whether you can smoothly sell it. @termmax  I recognize this ledger. The rewards can be lively, sure—but if I take a smaller position, I’ll sleep better at night. #TermMax  #BTC #ETH

Tonight my washer paused mid-spin, and the Wi‑Fi started spinning too. At the same time I was repeatedly refreshing a browser in the Dusk zone; when the interval between a few blocks stretched, my first reaction was: “Please don’t tell me something else happened to the chain.” Later, after rereading the whitepaper’s Chapter 3, I realized I’d only looked at the smooth-flow scenarios before—what’s really worth watching is how the system wraps things up when the network is at its ugliest. @Dusk_Foundation 

Succinct Attestation normally goes through three steps each round: proposal, verification, and approval. If a large number of Provisioners are offline or isolated, continuous iteration may fail to obtain candidate blocks or reach the required quorum. The failure path in the whitepaper is quite specific: once continuous failures hit the then-configured 16 times, it enters Emergency Mode. The step timeout then kicks in, allowing multiple “open iterations” to keep waiting for candidate blocks and quorum votes. The benefit is that the chain doesn’t easily just lie down; the cost is that multiple iterations may simultaneously form candidate forks.

Then Fallback prioritizes selecting blocks with lower iteration numbers; if needed, it falls back to another local chain. Rolling Finality then splits blocks into four tiers: accepted, attested, confirmed, and final. What really gets me is this: an accepted block doesn’t mean the money has fully settled in the bank yet. If there are n iterations with unknown outcomes before it, an accepted block typically still needs 2n consecutive attested or confirmed successor blocks before the risk gradually converges. RWA and securities clearing hate it when “the page succeeds, but the account can still be flipped.” So these rules are more substantial than a slogan like “instant finality.”

But I won’t just pick the comforting parts either. In extreme cases, an empty Emergency Block must be requested by a majority of stakers, and a Dusk node must sign out a new seed. This preserves liveness, while also leaving an emergency-trust assumption. I won’t deny $DUSK  because of this, and I definitely won’t hype it into something invincible; at least the failure, fallback, and trade-offs are all laid out on the table. For a life-preserving player like me, how to brake in bad weather matters more than how fast it runs on a sunny day. #dusk  #BTC #ETH
