What kept me researching this time was how it manages to nail the transaction down.

The SA consensus isn’t that all nodes chant “agree” together. In each round, a single block producer is selected via deterministic random sampling, then two committees are selected for verification and approval. They complete the proposal, verification, and approval steps in sequence. Eligibility is assigned by staking weight, but the score is generated from the previous block’s seed, the round, and the step. The new seed comes from the block producer’s signature on the previous seed, so the committees can’t be easily predicted ahead of time. That’s genuinely better than “high performance.”

What I kept thinking about is that voting doesn’t just cram a pile of signatures onto the chain. For BLS aggregated committee signatures, a bitset marks participants, and then it forms an attestation. When the network is congested and competing blocks show up, there are also fallback and rolling finality; a block goes through accepted, attested, confirmed, and finally final. A webpage popping up a “success” doesn’t mean the money has already been locked away in a safe.

Applied to the hotly debated tokenized securities and RWA, price flickering a bit is tolerable, but settlement bouncing around is not. I think Dusk’s selling point is that it turns finality into a verifiable process. But a beautiful whitepaper doesn’t mean institutions line up immediately—I still need to keep watching the real blocks. I used to misunderstand something: if you put a higher Gas limit on, you’ll be charged more DUSK.

Today I finally noticed from the Dusk fee breakdown that the Gas limit is more like an upper budget limit—it isn’t the final bill. What Dusk actually charges is the amount of Gas that the transaction truly uses, multiplied by the Gas price. Any unused Gas is not charged.

This seems small, but it directly changes how I operate. Before, if I was worried about high fees, I would unconsciously set the limit very tightly. But if the transaction runs halfway and then finds the Gas is insufficient, the operation rolls back. Still, the Gas already consumed has to be paid in DUSK. The result is nothing gets done, and the fee isn’t zero.#ETH  

So on Dusk, saving Gas doesn’t mean setting the limit to be just barely enough. The more practical approach is: first check the wallet’s estimate, leave a bit of headroom for execution, and then verify whether the Gas price is reasonable. The limit prevents accidental runaways, but the final spending depends on how much work that transaction actually performs.

Because of this, I also understand better why $DUSK  isn’t just a transaction code. On Dusk mainnet, both transfers and on-chain execution are paid in DUSK fees, and those fees go into block rewards. Someone uses the network, fees are generated; Provisioners participate in consensus, and rewards have a source. This relationship is much more concrete than just saying “the token has a purpose.”

Of course, setting a very high Gas limit isn’t without limits either. Your wallet balance must be sufficient to cover the fees the transaction could require, and an excessively high Gas price will likewise increase the actual cost. I’m now more willing to view these two things separately: the limit determines the maximum amount of work allowed, while the price determines how much you’re willing to pay per unit of work.#BTC  

Sun Quan wouldn’t only send half the rations just because he’s afraid of running out. You can set an upper limit for the budget, but you still have to make sure the military order can be carried out in full.

When you send a Dusk transaction, do you set the Gas limit tightly, or do you leave it some extra headroom?#dusk  $DUSK  @Dusk_Foundation

这件事看起来很小，却会直接改变我的操作。以前怕费用高，我会下意识把上限压得很紧。可一旦交易执行到一半发现Gas不够，操作会回滚，前面已经消耗的Gas仍然要用DUSK支付。结果就是事情没办成，费用也不是零。#ETH  

所以在Dusk上，省Gas不等于把上限卡到刚刚好。更实际的做法，是先看钱包给出的预估，给执行留一点余量，再检查Gas price是否合理。上限负责防止意外失控，最终支出仍取决于这笔交易真正做了多少工作。

我也因此更容易理解$DUSK 为什么不只是一个交易代码。Dusk主网上的转账和链上执行都用DUSK支付费用，这些费用会进入区块奖励。有人使用网络，费用产生；Provisioner参与共识，奖励才有来源。这条关系比一句“代币有用途”具体得多。

当然，填很高的Gas limit也不是完全没有边界，钱包余额必须覆盖交易可能需要的费用，Gas price过高同样会抬高实际成本。我现在更愿意把两件事分开看：limit决定最多允许做多少工作，price决定每单位工作愿意付多少。#BTC  

孙权调兵不会因为怕耗粮，就只发半程口粮。预算可以设上限，但要先保证军令能执行完。

你发Dusk交易时，会把Gas上限压得很紧，还是给它留一点余量？#dusk  $DUSK  @Dusk_Foundation

This isn’t guesswork—it turns the July-approved law into executable details. Medium term: the real impact of this rule is the stablecoin landscape. Stablecoins are the foundation of the crypto market—when the foundation is more stable, there are more reasons for institutions to enter.

Clear direction: bullish. Turning regulation into implementation is 100 times better than regulation hanging in uncertainty. What the market fears most isn’t stricter rules—it’s having no rules. Going downstairs to buy coffee at night, I stared at the fixed QR code on the counter and suddenly thought: in real life, having a single code repeatedly receive payments is convenient. But if I copy that habit directly onto a public chain, it’s like turning the transaction stream into a continuous TV series—so that strangers can follow from episode one all the way to the finale.

After I got home, I ran a few rounds of transfers in the Dusk test environment. I didn’t rush to check TPS, and I didn’t stare at the charts for comfort. Instead, I specifically compared the whitepaper’s Section 6.4 to study stealth addresses. It doesn’t mean reusing the same public address over and over. First, the payee provides the public spending key (A, B). Each time, the sender generates a random number r, then computes a one-time public key pk = Hposeidon(rA)G + B, and also attaches R = rG. The payee scans with the viewing key (a, B), verifying whether pk equals Hposeidon(Ra)G + B. When it’s time to actually spend, there’s still a secret amount b that generates the corresponding spending key.

What struck me most about this design isn’t the words “privacy.” It’s that permissions are split: being able to recognize which outputs belong to you doesn’t mean you’re allowed to transfer the funds away. Put bluntly, the accounting key and the safe key aren’t the same key. For assets like securities and RWA—things that must remain confidential yet still leave room for audits—this kind of boundary is far more practical than a slogan like “fully anonymous.”

That said, I won’t declare it invincible just because it’s a stealth address. Network metadata, usage habits, and frontend exposure can still leak information. @Dusk_Foundation  is worth watching because it turns one-time addresses, viewing rights, and spending rights into a complete cryptographic workflow, rather than just draping an ordinary transfer with a layer of black cloth. $DUSK  I’ll keep observing—technology can preserve privacy, but operational mistakes won’t. #dusk  #BTC #ETH

晚上下楼买咖啡，我盯着柜台那张固定收款码，突然想到：现实里一个码反复收钱很方便，可把这习惯原样搬上公链，等于主动把流水拍成连续剧，陌生人还能从第一集追到大结局。

这套设计最戳我的不是“隐私”两个字，而是权限被拆开了：能识别哪些输出属于自己，不代表有权把钱转走。说粗一点，查账钥匙和保险柜钥匙不是同一把。对证券、RWA这类既要保密又要留审计空间的资产，这种边界比一句“完全匿名”实用得多。

不过我不会因为一个隐身地址就喊无敌，网络元数据、使用习惯和前端暴露照样可能泄密。@Dusk_Foundation  值得盯的，是把一次性地址、查看权限与花费权限做成完整密码学流程，而不是给普通转账套层黑布。$DUSK 我继续观察，技术能保密，操作失误可不会。#dusk  #BTC #ETH

Sometimes the strangest thing isn’t that good news comes out and people rush in—it’s that someone is already frantically hoarding, while the chart looks calm and quiet.

This time, Bitmine bought ETH close to 4.8% of the total supply it holds. If this happened with other coins, sentiment would’ve exploded already.

But now the $ETH  is still churning around $1906, up only about 1.2% over the past 24 hours.

When I glanced at it while blow-drying my hair in front of the vanity, I really couldn’t hold it together.😂

This feels like smart money is moving inventory slowly, while the surface intentionally makes you feel like, “It’s already too late” isn’t happening.

I’m not saying it’s about to take off immediately.

What I mean is that this level of sustained accumulation, if the market still isn’t excited, actually suggests the chips haven’t reached the hottest stage yet.

What makes me even more uncomfortable is the derivatives side.

The $ETH  contract volume is already 15.6 times that of the spot market—it looks exhausting just watching it.

That indicates there are too many people trading around it right now. A lot of them aren’t really buying—they’re betting on which direction the next move will go.

A market like this is the easiest to wash out the chasers until they start questioning their sanity.

So my view is very clear: I’m biased bullish on $ETH , but I don’t want to chase the pump too aggressively.

If I really do it, I’d rather wait for it to pull back a bit and then enter, or try with a light position slowly.

The news is somewhat positive, and the position isn’t particularly high, but the market sentiment hasn’t fully caught up yet. I’ll look at this mismatch a couple more times.

When it’s 1 or 2 a.m. and you’re staring at the candlestick chart alone, the worst thing isn’t missing the chance—it’s misreading “slowly getting stronger” as “it’s over.”

I might be wrong too—just my judgment. $ETH #ETH

Then one single candle surged on high volume, pushing up to 1900—690,000 lots, which is five times the average volume in the prior period. After that, it didn’t come back down. It held its ground.

On the order book, 1868 is the lowest point of this move. After it was smashed down, price quickly snapped back, showing there’s support underneath. Now price is around 1905, just under ten points away from the 24h high of 1914.85. It didn’t break straight through, but it also didn’t retreat. This level feels a bit “up in the air,” yet the bias is still upward. From 1868 to 1914, the rebound is less than 3%. It doesn’t sound big, but after consecutive low-volume, sideways consolidation, the significance is different.

Market sentiment is rather cold. The funding rate is 0.0039%, extremely low—almost negligible. Very few people who go long open leverage, and no one is rushing to add positions. In the last 24 hours, spot-for-futures volume is $5.2 billion, which isn’t particularly active when you compare it to ETH. In this kind of situation, it’s actually healthy. Everyone’s scared, so the move probably isn’t over. When it truly turns manic, the funding rate will spike to above 0.1%, and then comes the harvest.

The big players are quietly building positions. That high-volume bullish candle wasn’t done by retail. A 690,000-lot 4h trading volume corresponds to a $1.3 billion transaction value. Retail can’t coordinate with that kind of force. The large players absorbed the chips from between 1875 and 1890, pushed the price above 1900, and then paused. They’re not in a hurry to push further, which suggests either the position isn’t fully built yet, or they’re waiting for a better entry to add.

The mark price is almost the same as the current price, with no obvious premium or discount—this indicates that the futures market and the spot market are moving in sync.

Looking at the volume-price structure: during the breakout candle with high volume, price moved from 1875 to 1900, and the volume-price alignment is fine. After that, the next three 4h candles stayed above 1900, while volume gradually shrank into the 300,000–600,000 range—this looks like a low-volume pullback for confirmation. As volume contracts and price doesn’t fall, it suggests the chips are being locked in well. If it were to pull back and expand volume, that would be a dangerous signal. In the 24h transaction value of $5.2 billion, half of it is concentrated in the breakout leg—showing that main capital is acting at the key level.

On the candlestick details: the most recent 4h candle is a small bearish one—opened at 1906 and closed at 1905, with very little movement. There’s a top wick up to 1914, which implies some sell pressure, but not heavy. The big bullish candle body from 1875 to 1900 now has price trading completely above the body—this is a strong sign. After the low at 1868, several candles with lower wicks kept closing; every time price got smashed down, someone stepped in to absorb.

I’m bullish. The bottom support is clear; the breakout on high volume is valid; and the low-volume confirmation looks healthy. The low funding rate suggests there’s still room. 1900 is the new support level—if it doesn’t break, I’ll keep looking for higher prices.

量价结构看，突破那根放量的同时价格从1875拉到1900，量价配合没问题。之后三根4h都在1900以上，成交量逐步缩小到30万到60万区间，属于缩量回踩确认。量缩价不跌，筹码锁定良好。如果回踩放量，那才是危险信号。24h成交额52亿美金里，有一半集中在突破那一段，说明主力资金集中在关键位置出手。

K线细节上，最近一根4h收小阴，开盘1906收盘1905，波动很小。上影到1914，有抛压但不重。前面大阳线实体在1875到1900之间，现在价格完全在实体上方运行，这是强势特征。1868那个低点之后连续收了几根带下影的线，每次砸下去都有人接。

【The #1 reason retail traders lose money isn’t getting the direction wrong—it’s poor position management】

Many people think they’re “trading” coins, but in reality they’re “gambling”—when it drops, they stubbornly hold to death; when it rises, they can’t hold on. This kind of operation has been especially obvious in ETH’s recent 7-day market.

Let’s start with the data: +1.2% in 24 hours, +1.6% in 7 days. It doesn’t look exciting, but if you look closely at the chart, in the range between 1830 and 1950, ETH has been oscillating narrowly for nearly a week. Trading volume is active, meaning both bulls and bears are entering the market, but neither side has been able to knock the other out. This is the most frustrating kind of market—and also the time when retail traders are most likely to make mistakes.

The Fear & Greed Index is 31, with a weekly average of 30. Market sentiment is extremely pessimistic. But I noticed an interesting pattern: historically, every time the FNG falls into this range, ETH is almost always at a stage-wise bottom. This time? I can’t promise anything, but from a payout-odds perspective, the downside room looks limited.

Bitmine’s Tom Lee bought nearly 10,000 more ETH, and his holdings now account for 4.8% of circulating supply. What’s interesting here isn’t how much he bought—it’s why he’s buying at this position. Institutions aren’t charities; they’ve already done the math.

ETH’s fundamentals are changing. The Hegotá upgrade with 60+ proposals is underway, including important privacy fixes. I’ve said many times: technological iterations may not affect price in the short term, but in the long run, they will definitely be reflected in valuation.

What to watch next week? Trading volume. At the end of a range-bound move, volume is key—if it breaks out with volume beyond 1951, it would mean the bulls finally can’t hold back; if volume keeps shrinking, then it may have to grind on.

Has my view changed this week? Honestly, it’s become more cautious. It’s not because I don’t have confidence in ETH—it’s because I’m still observing the overall liquidity environment. A bull market won’t arrive all at once, and a bear market won’t bottom out just in one go.

Let’s be practical: are you still doing DCA right now? Or have you already been ground out by this chop?

【散户亏钱的第一大原因，不是方向看错，而是仓位管理】

很多人以为自己在"炒"币，其实是在"赌"币——跌了死扛，涨了拿不住。这种操作在ETH最近7天的行情里表现得特别明显。

先说数据：24小时+1.2%，7天+1.6%。看着不刺激，但你仔细看盘面——在1830到1950这个区间里，ETH已经窄幅震荡了将近一周。成交量活跃，说明多空都在进场，但谁也没能把对方打趴下。这种行情最磨人，也是散户最容易犯错的时候。

恐惧贪婪指数31，周均30。市场情绪极度悲观，但我反而注意到一个有意思的现象：历史上每次FNG到这个区间，ETH几乎都是阶段性底部。这次呢？我不敢打包票，但从赔率角度看，向下的空间已经有限了。

Bitmine的Tom Lee又买了将近一万枚ETH，现在持仓占流通量的4.8%。这事儿有意思的地方在哪？不是他买了多少，而是为什么在这个位置还在买。机构不是慈善机构，人家算过账的。

ETH的基本面在变，Hegotá升级60多个提案在路上，包括重要的隐私修复。我说过很多次，技术迭代短期不影响价格，但长期一定会在估值上体现。

下周盯什么？成交量。震荡区间末端，量能是关键——能放量突破1951，说明多方终于憋不住了；要是继续缩量，那可能还得磨。

这周我的判断变过吗？说实话，变得更谨慎了。不是对ETH没信心，是对整体流动性环境还在观察。牛市不会一蹴而就，熊市也不会一次见底。

说个实在的：你现在还在定投吗？还是已经被磨出去了？

Because positions that are “only a little bit away” are the easiest to whip up emotions.

$ETH  is still hovering above 1908 today, and it really is very close to the upper edge of the cloud.

But the problem is: close doesn’t mean it’s through.

【The script of 2018—this time, they changed the actor】

At the end of the 2018 bear market, who was buying? The first DeFi participants and private funds were slowly accumulating positions with chips that cost almost nothing.
Now in 2025, who is buying? Tom Lee’s Bitmine has been continuously sweeping the market over the past few months, already holding nearly 5% of Ethereum’s circulating supply.
What about the price? It’s still grinding around the $1,900 mark. The FNG Fear & Greed Index is 41, slightly higher than the weekly average of 32—so the market isn’t as hopeless as people imagine.

So what does this mean? Smart money is building positions against the trend, while retail investors are still waiting for “something lower.”

I mentioned before that at this ETH level, the core issue isn’t price—it’s the supply-and-demand structure quietly changing. This week, Bitmine bought nearly ten thousand more ETH. The action itself isn’t new, but the 5% figure is interesting: a non–DeFi-native institution going long ETH in one direction isn’t retail behavior—this looks like someone is treating ETH like a corporate bond to allocate.

What does it mean in concrete terms?

When 5% of the circulating supply is concentrated in one company, who will be affected?

First, the future selling-pressure curve changes. Bitmine is a treasury company, not a retail trader. It doesn’t chase pumps or kill swings, but its lock-up logic is completely different from that of retail.
The $ 287M annualized staking returns don’t sound like much, but that’s calculated based on the current price. If the coin price rises, the dollar value of staking rewards expands, turning into a positive feedback loop—a reason to hold.

Second, in the Hegotá upgrade, the privacy improvement package may sound technical, but it targets real demand: institutions want to settle on-chain without being fully transparent. Compliant buyers entering the market need this underlying infrastructure. This isn’t hype—it’s a real function someone is developing.

Is the business logic sound? It is. But there’s a prerequisite: ETH can’t stay range-bound at this level for too long. Institutions have patience; retail doesn’t. Liquidity will start to split.

Has my view changed this week? Honestly, before writing this piece I was a bit hesitant, but after seeing Bitmine continue buying and the sentiment index climb from 32 to 41— the market is slowly regaining some confidence. This signal is more honest than the candlestick chart.

Do you think this combination of “smart money building positions against the trend + expectations of fundamental upgrades” can lead to a different kind of bottom this time?

【2018年的剧本，这次换了个演员】

2018年熊市末尾，谁在买？第一批DeFi玩家，私募基金，用几乎为零的成本筹码慢慢收筹码。
2025年的现在，谁在买？Tom Lee的Bitmine，过去几个月持续扫货，手里已经攥住了将近5%的以太坊流通量。
价格呢？还在1900刀附近磨。FNG恐慌贪婪指数41，比周均32高一点，市场其实没有想象中那么绝望。

这说明什么？聪明的钱在逆势建仓，散户还在等"更低"。

我之前说过，ETH在这位置，核心矛盾不是价格，是供需结构在悄悄改变。这周Bitmine又买了将近一万个ETH，这个动作本身不算新鲜，但5%这个数字有意思了——一个非DeFi原生机构，单边做多ETH，这不是散户行为，这是有人把ETH当企业债在配置。

落到实处意味着什么？

5%的流通量集中在一家公司手里，谁会受影响？

第一，未来的抛压曲线变了。Bitmine是 treasury company，不是散户，它不追涨杀跌，但它的锁仓逻辑和散户完全不同。$ 287M的年化质押收益听着不多，但那是基于当前价格算的，币价一涨，质押收益的美元价值就膨胀，变成一个正循环的持有理由。

第二，Hegotá升级里那个隐私改进包，名字听着技术，但它对准的是真实需求——机构想在链上结算但不想全透明。合规买家进场需要这个底层设施。这不是画饼，是有人在开发的真实功能。

商业逻辑通不通？通。但有个前提：ETH不能在这位置横太久。机构有耐心，散户没有，流动性会分化。

这周我的看法有变过吗？说实话，来写这篇之前我还有点犹豫，但看到Bitmine继续买、情绪指数从32爬到41——市场在慢慢找回一点信心，这信号比K线诚实。

你觉得这种"聪明钱逆势建仓+基本面升级预期"的组合，这次能走出不一样的底部吗？

Geopolitical Oil-Price Disruptions and ETF Inflows Coexist as Bitcoin Trades in a Tight Range

In recent times, Bitcoin has continued to move within a relatively narrow trading band, with subdued market activity and insufficient one-way momentum. Based on the information that has been disclosed, on the one hand, after the Middle East-related ceasefire arrangements expire, shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has nearly come to a standstill, leading to a repricing of oil supply and the risk of upside oil prices. On the other hand, there are signs that capital flows into U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs are improving; the earlier period of institutional net outflows has been eased. With external macro disruptions and internal changes in capital structure occurring at the same time, the market has shown more of a range-bound pattern than a trend-based breakout.

In terms of event background, the Strait of Hormuz, as a critical global oil transportation route, has seen a sharp drop in traffic compared with normal levels. Shipping data indicates that the number of vessels transiting over the weekend fell significantly. Disrupted strait traffic has prompted the market to reassess the supply-shock transmission path. Oil prices subsequently strengthened, and Brent crude briefly approached the high end of the recent range. If oil prices continue to rise, it could reinforce expectations of sticky inflation and affect the pace of easing monetary policy in major economies—an important external variable that has constrained upside room for crypto assets since this summer. Separately, earlier-published U.S. inflation data showed that both headline and core readings broadly matched expectations. While the risk of runaway inflation tail events declined, “meeting expectations” itself did not provide a strong enough catalyst for repricing rate cuts, and the crypto market’s reaction was relatively muted.

On the core facts, within the reporting range, the Bitcoin price mostly hovered around the $63,000 area and repeatedly faced resistance just below $64,000. Risk assets rose in tandem on some trading days, and gold, silver, and portions of the technology growth sector also showed strength. On the capital side, some institutions noted that during the statistical sample period, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded continuous net subscriptions. As of the third quarter to date, net inflows have improved markedly compared with the sharp net outflows seen in the latter half of the second quarter. Meanwhile, spot trading volume has fallen to multi-year lows, and both perpetual contract trading volume and volatility are also relatively low, suggesting insufficient participation enthusiasm. The U.S. Dollar Index has retreated to a phase low, which theoretically provides some support for U.S. dollar-denominated risk assets. At the corporate level, large holders such as Strategy supplemented cash through equity financing to maintain a stable total Bitcoin position, and publicly emphasized the need for flexibility in buying and selling Bitcoin to support confidence in preferred dividends and lending business—indicating that institutional behavior is becoming more finely tuned.

From a logic breakdown, current pricing resembles a combination of “macro tail risks not fully resolved” and “micro liquidity conditions quietly repairing.” Strait shipping and oil prices act as upward headwinds and volatility amplifiers. ETF inflows returning, thin trading, and a weaker dollar provide a cushion on the downside. Bitcoin’s muted reaction to some traditional inflation data also suggests the increasing weight of internal crypto supply-demand dynamics, regulatory expectations, and structural allocation forces, along with reduced short-term transmission efficiency from macro data. Large AI-computing orders and tech-sector sentiment have spillover effects on overall risk appetite, but they are unlikely to independently rewrite Bitcoin’s box structure.

Regarding the impact pathways for the crypto market: if the Hormuz situation pushes up oil prices and also drives U.S. Treasury yields and the dollar higher on a temporary basis, it could suppress risk appetite and keep Bitcoin capped near the upper end of its range. If transit and diplomatic signals ease, and ETF capital flows continue to return, that would favor upside repair elasticity after the consolidation. On leverage, despite the backdrop of contracting trading, open interest in perpetual contracts remains relatively elevated, so liquidity shocks in either direction may amplify short-term volatility.

The editor’s view is that, at this stage, it is more appropriate to interpret the trend as box consolidation during the summer liquidity lull. In terms of facts, prices are still subject to geopolitical and energy-price disruptions, but capital flows have shifted from net outflows to phase-level net inflows. In terms of speculation, when low volatility and low turnover coexist, the market appears more like it is waiting for new macro or policy catalysts rather than having already confirmed a trend reversal. Going forward, attention should focus on whether Strait transit, oil prices, and ETF subscriptions/redemptions can produce a synchronized push in the same direction, and whether policy communication windows lead to adjustments in rate-expectation assumptions—so as to avoid extrapolating any single piece of news linearly into a directional turning point.

近期比特币继续在相对狭窄的价格带内运行，市场交投偏淡，单边驱动不足。综合已披露信息，一方面中东相关休战安排到期后霍尔木兹海峡航运近乎停滞，石油供应与油价上行风险被重新定价；另一方面美国现货比特币ETF资金流向出现改善迹象，此前阶段性机构净流出压力有所缓和。外部宏观扰动与内部资金结构变化同时存在，使行情更多表现为区间震荡，而非趋势性突破。

事件背景上，霍尔木兹海峡作为全球重要石油运输通道，通行量较常年水平大幅下滑。有航运数据显示，周末通行船只显著减少，海峡交通受阻令市场重新评估供应冲击路径。油价随之走强，布伦特原油一度逼近阶段高位。油价若持续抬升，可能强化通胀粘性预期，并影响主要经济体货币政策宽松节奏，这是今年夏季以来制约加密资产上行空间的重要外部变量。另据较早前公布的美国通胀数据，整体与核心读数大体符合预期，通胀失控尾部风险下降，但“符合预期”本身并未提供足够强的降息重定价催化，加密市场反应亦相对平淡。

核心事实方面，比特币价格在报道区间内多徘徊于约六万三千美元一带，并反复受制于六万四千美元下方阻力；风险资产在部分交易日同步走高，黄金、白银与部分科技成长板块亦有表现。资金层面，有机构指出美国现货比特币ETF在统计样本期内出现连续净申购，第三季度迄今净流入状况相较二季度后半段大幅净流出已明显好转。与此同时，现货成交量降至多年低位，永续合约成交量与波动率亦处相对低位，显示市场参与热度不足。美元指数回落至阶段低点，理论上对以美元计价的风险资产构成一定支撑。企业端，Strategy等大型持仓主体通过股权融资补充现金、维持比特币持仓总量稳定，并公开强调需具备买卖比特币的灵活性以支持优先股分红与信贷业务信心，说明机构行为模式更趋精细化。

逻辑拆解看，当前定价更接近“宏观尾部风险未解除、微观资金面悄然修复”的组合。海峡航运与油价构成上行阻力与波动放大器；ETF回流、成交清淡与美元走弱则提供下方缓冲。比特币对部分传统通胀数据反应偏钝，侧面说明加密市场内部供需、监管预期与结构性配置力量的权重上升，宏观数据的短线传导效率下降。人工智能算力大单与科技股情绪对整体风险偏好存在外溢，但难以单独改写比特币的箱体结构。

对加密市场的影响路径上，若霍尔木兹局势推高油价并带动美债收益率与美元阶段性走强，可能压制风险偏好，使比特币继续受制于区间上沿；若通行与外交信号缓和，叠加ETF资金延续回流，则有利于盘整后的修复弹性。杠杆方面，永续合约未平仓量在成交萎缩背景下仍相对偏高，任一方向的流动性冲击都可能放大短线波动。

编辑判断认为，现阶段更宜将走势理解为夏季流动性淡季中的箱体整理：事实层面，价格仍受地缘与能源价格扰动，但资金流向已从净流出转向阶段性净流入；推测层面，低波动与低成交并存时，市场更像在等待新的宏观或政策催化，而非已经确认趋势反转。后续应重点跟踪海峡通行、油价与ETF申赎能否形成同向共振，以及政策沟通窗口对利率预期的修正，避免把单一新闻线性外推为方向性拐点。

#dusk $DUSK @Dusk_Foundation Recently, I did a deep retrospective on the new system $DUSK  and uncovered a major cognitive misconception. In the past, I always thought: since it claims to be a privacy chain, operations across the entire network would automatically vanish into the dark. But after breaking down its three-layer architecture, the truth becomes clear—its “anonymity” feature is not a default, global on/off switch.

At the infrastructure layer, DuskDS handles the core hard parts like consensus confirmation and data availability. But once it comes to ledger bookkeeping, the routes begin to diverge: 
• Transparent ledger flow: it goes through the Moonlight system, where accounts are fully public just like on traditional chains.
• Hidden ledger flow: it switches into the Phoenix mechanism, where assets are tokenized into protected notes.
Zero-knowledge proofs quietly do the heavy lifting here—preventing double-spends while also blurring specific amounts and transaction destinations. Clearly, the confidentiality mechanism is embedded only in specific models, not crudely overriding the whole network.

The fragmentation at the contract layer is even more pronounced. To align with the Ethereum ecosystem’s developer community, the official created DuskEVM. But once you’re operating in the world of EVM—a global state machine—if you want to invoke privacy, you must plug in an auxiliary top-layer protocol like the Hedger. That’s rather cumbersome. If you want a seamless experience with pure ZK performance, you still have to rely on its direct descendant, DuskVM. This shows the team’s core logic isn’t simply “everything is hidden.” Instead, transparency, privacy, and execution libraries are treated as independent modules, assembled at the application layer as needed.

The greater the combination space you provide, the heavier the burden of controlling data granularity falls on developers. For today’s booming RWA (real-world assets), when you look at projects like this in the future, don’t obsess over whether any single transaction’s flow can be concealed. The real touchstone is this: when a whole set of complex financial logic is interleaved and routed back and forth across DuskDS, DuskVM, and DuskEVM, can it keep the confidentiality perimeter locked down—tight with no leakage at the seams? That is the most hardcore technical test coming next.$ETH #eth

I used to think that since it markets privacy, the confidentiality capabilities baked into its core code should be shared across the whole network. #termmax @termmax After finishing the 2026 TMX Whitepaper, I reached a completely new judgment about TermMax’s business logic. I used to think FT and XT were just accounting vouchers used inside lending protocols, but after thinking it through, I realized this mechanism is actually a fine-grained slicing of debt. FT specifically strips out the fixed maturity payoff that must be settled at maturity, and only together with XT does it make up the full debt size. In effect, this turns future capital usage costs into a chip that can be independently traded. The cleverest part is that it gives users back full control.

The rollout of V2 is the key turning point where the entire model changes qualitatively. Now every lending market supports placing Limit Orders directly. Lenders can set a minimum return for themselves, while borrowers can cap the interest rate they are willing to pay. Then TermMax App V2 acts as the hub, consolidating retail orders and Range Orders deployed by Curators, and settling them in batches.

The core shift here is that interest rates are no longer rigid numbers calculated by the system according to a formula and passively accepted by you; instead, they become bid and ask quotes that can be called out from the start. FT and XT provide the underlying spot instruments, Limit Orders handle price quoting, and the Aggregator serves as the matching engine. With this combination, it really does seem to be reaching the threshold of a decentralized interest rate trading market.

That said, I’m not blindly optimistic either. The risks are still obvious: having many quoted orders does not mean market pricing is accurate. If order book depth is too thin, the execution price swept by the Aggregator may just be the best among the mediocre options available at the moment, and hardly a fair reflection of the market’s true cost of capital.

So for now, I still won’t call it a proper interest rate exchange. We need to wait and see. We need to keep watching whether different maturities can produce a smooth term structure curve, whether order book quotes can sustain real, hard-fought competition, and finally compare the spread between FT’s spot price and floating interest rates to see whether the logic really holds up under scrutiny.#eth $ETH

V2 版本的落地是整个模式发生质变的关键节点。现在每一个借贷盘口都支持直接挂 Limit Order。放款方能给自己兜一个收益底线，借钱方能划定一个利息上限。紧接着，TermMax App V2 会充当枢纽，把散户丢进去的挂单与 Curator 部署的 Range Order 统一归集，然后进行批量结算。

#termmax @termmax I re-examined the TMX Whitepaper for the 2026 version, and my understanding of TermMax got refreshed. What makes this project so compelling isn’t that it locks in interest rates—it’s that it returns to retail traders the power to decide what the capital is actually worth. At first, I instinctively treated FT and XT as ordinary receipts from the pool. But now I see that this is a very sophisticated debt-structuring technique. FT is separated on its own as the fixed, non-negotiable baseline return—it only becomes a complete receivable when paired with XT. With this slicing, the time-occupancy fee for future capital naturally turns into an underlying asset that can be traded anytime on the secondary market.

What fully flipped my mindset was the new mechanism introduced with V2. As of now, each borrowing/lending asset supports placing it directly as a Limit Order. The “water-release” guys can hold a minimum yield floor, while the borrowers can set a hard ceiling on their cost. Then, TermMax App V2 acts as the clearing hub: it absorbs the Range Orders laid out by the Curator and all the one-off orders from retail traders, combining them into centralized packages.

The chemical reaction caused by this logic is very straightforward: interest has moved on from the old passive situation where the system calculates it and you can only accept it. It has evolved into a trump card that can be visibly identified before entering the market. FT and XT build the spot foundation; Limit Orders serve as the instruments for the game; and the Aggregator is the matching engine that scans the entire field for the optimal solution. Objectively speaking, this playbook has already shaken off the quicksand of traditional lending. The outline of a decentralized interest-rate corridor is now quite clear.

Still, I keep half my mind sharp when monitoring the order book. Just because calls and shouts are lively doesn’t mean the pricing is precise. Suppose the real depth of the order book can’t keep up—then the execution prices matched by the Aggregator are very likely to be locally distorted “pseudo-fair values,” which can’t represent the true capital levels in the broader market.

So it’s still too early to slap a “interest-rate exchange” label on it. The focus going forward is clear: can different cycles run through a reasonable yield structure? Is there genuine, sustained price competition in the order-placing area? And can the FT displayed price versus the floating interest-rate spread outside stay within a logically self-consistent range? #eth $ETH

#termmax @termmax 重新复盘了 2026 版的 TMX Whitepaper，我对 TermMax 的认知经历了一次刷新。这项目最抓人的点，不在于锁死利息，而是把“资金到底值多少钱”的拍板权交还给了散户。刚开始，我习惯性地把 FT 和 XT 当作池子里的普通收据。但现在看，这是一种极高明的债务解构手法。FT 单独剥离了雷打不动的保底回报，它配合 XT 才算拼出一笔完整的债权。通过这种切分，未来资金的时间占用费，就顺理成章地转化成了能随时在二级倒腾的标的。

促使我彻底转变思路的，是 V2 上线的新机制。当下，每一个借贷标的都支持直接丢 Limit Order。放水的老哥可以死守一个收益下限，拿钱的则能卡死一个成本天花板。紧接着，TermMax App V2 会扮演清算枢纽，把 Curator 铺展的 Range Order 和散户的散单全盘吸纳，捏合在一起集中打包。

这套逻辑引发的化学反应非常直观：利息告别了以往“系统一算、你只能认”的被动局面，进化成了进场前就能明牌亮出的底牌。FT 和 XT 搭建了现货底座，Limit Order 充当了博弈工具，而 Aggregator 则是满场找最优解的撮合引擎。客观讲，这套打法已经甩开了传统借贷的泥潭，一条去中心化利率走廊的轮廓相当清晰。

但我看盘习惯留一半清醒。喊单热闹，不意味着定价就精准。假设盘口的真实厚度跟不上，Aggregator 匹配出的成交价，极有可能是局部失真的“伪公允”，代表不了大环境真实的资金水位。

因此，现在给它贴上“利率交易所”的标签还太早。后续盯盘的重点很明确：不同周期能不能跑通一条合理的收益结构？挂单区有没有真金白银的持续火拼？还有，FT 的盘面价跟外头的浮动利率差值，能不能稳在一个逻辑自洽的区间内？#eth $ETH

Core Ethereum developers, while discussing the next main upgrade, have officially listed “privacy” as a candidate direction. Simply put: they want ordinary users’ transfers to no longer be fully exposed to the entire network. Right now, every action in your wallet can be looked up by anyone with a browser. If the change goes live, default anonymity would be greatly improved, but the trade-off is reduced on-chain transparency—and the probability of being targeted by regulatory bodies would rise at the same time.

The fact that Tornado Cash was sanctioned proves that centralized privacy solutions are a dead end—protocol-level privacy is the way out. #termmax @termmax  Lately I’ve been staring at on-chain data every day—the loan interest rates that swing like a roller coaster really make my head spin. I often think: since everyone is trading crypto so hard, why can’t the borrowing interest be separated out and listed directly for matching? After flipping through TermMax’s whitepaper right before the TGE, I found they actually did exactly that. The project team split a loan into two parts: the principal and the interest, and took the interest out as the trading asset. The big whales who provide liquidity take away the guaranteed “principal note,” while brothers who want to add positions have to sell the “interest note” in advance to lock in the cost. This kind of move turns messy books into a game where the outcome is decided from the start—it really has something.

The key highlight all lies in V2’s matching mechanism. Previously, what I hated most about lending pools was that slippage would eat your profits. Now it’s a real, no-nonsense reveal of the cards. Set an interest-rate ceiling for borrowers, and have lenders bite tightly at a minimum yield floor. The two sides then purely “duel” with limit orders—no more gimmicks. This is ruthless: it essentially blasts apart the traditional pool-based model that optimizes capital utilization and completely rewires it into something like the order book you see in spot trading for $BTC, where what you see is what you get.

But then again, this system can run into weird problems in extreme market conditions. Everyone is coldly placing orders—if the market crashes and sentiment gets smashed, the order book can be drained in an instant, making it easy to blow out interest rates that are totally out of bounds. It’s like those leveraged derivative toys on-chain from the earlier days—$ETH —where they look like fixed costs, but you can’t escape the stampede during chain-liquidation. The trade that executes fastest on the screen is very likely just bloody collateral, and it won’t be accurate.

So for this round, my strategy is very clear: after TMX launches its token, I will never rush in first. Let the market fight it out on the inside for a while. Then we’ll see whether this order-book-style system can hold up through the churn of needles poking up and down, and whether it can actually form a truly reliable interest-rate curve on-chain. If this foundation really holds firm, then the old rules in DeFi lending might genuinely be ready to be thrown out the window. #ETH $ETH

Even more impressive is the risk-control logic of $DUSK : it hard-codes forced freezing and permission blocking directly into the protocol layer. Once a violation occurs, the issuer can liquidate assets on-chain immediately. That directly targets the pain point of traditional financial custody. Of course, this kind of built-in centralized management leaves an unmistakable centralized “stamp,” which definitely shatters the early $ETH  geeks’ ideals—so it’s completely normal that longtime players feel uneasy.

In short, Dusk chose an extremely niche yet logically airtight path. The early-morning play: BTC is above 64,500, and ETH is holding at 1,913.

It’s up 2.5%, and a lot of people are getting excited. But what I see isn’t the increase—I see a BEAR_RECOVERY structure, and a CHOP_MID ETH that’s stuck in place, treading water.

━━━ What the market is saying right now ━━━
BTC is crawling over the rubble of a bear market—it isn’t a bull-market kickoff. BEAR_RECOVERY means: something that was knocked down is trying to stand back up. In this kind of structure, every green candle needs a solid reason. Otherwise, it can be dragged back at any moment.

ETH is more honest—CHOP_MID is the classic “I don’t know whether to go up or down.” When BTC moves, ETH only moves along for a bit. It doesn’t show independent strength.

━━━ Psychological layer ━━━
In this kind of market, the easiest problem to run into isn’t your analysis—it’s your discipline. Seeing price rise makes you want to add; seeing ETH lag makes you want to chase. Fear and greed fuse here into something more dangerous: impulsiveness.

A real trader isn’t the one who runs fast—it’s the one who doesn’t move at the wrong time.

━━━ Strategy reference ━━━
If you’re already holding BTC and the structure hasn’t been broken, hold your position. If you want to chase, wait for the pullback and confirmation—don’t buy the spike. With ETH’s CHOP setup, keep exposure light and observe; don’t let it drain your patience and capital.

The best trade today might be doing nothing.

title: LIQUIDEZ DO FED E CRIPTO: POR QUE MAIS DINHEIRO NO SISTEMA PODE AJUDAR BTC E ALTCOINS
subTitle:
💧 LIQUIDEZ DO FED E CRIPTO: POR QUE MAIS DINHEIRO NO SISTEMA PODE AJUDAR BTC E ALTCOINS
Quando se fala em liquidez do Federal Reserve, a lógica é relativamente simples: quanto mais dinheiro circulando no sistema financeiro e menor o estresse de liquidez, maior tende a ser o apetite por risco.
E como Bitcoin e criptomoedas ainda são tratados pelo mercado como ativos de risco, esse ambiente pode favorecer o setor.
📈 COMO A LIQUIDEZ PODE AFETAR A CRIPTO
💰 Mais liquidez = mais disposição para assumir risco
Quando as condições financeiras ficam menos apertadas, parte do capital tende a procurar ativos com maior potencial de retorno. Isso pode beneficiar ações de tecnologia, Bitcoin e, em determinados momentos, altcoins.

📉 Yields e dólar também importam
Se os rendimentos dos Treasuries aliviam e o dólar perde força, a pressão sobre ativos de risco pode diminuir. Não é uma relação automática, mas é um dos principais canais observados pelo mercado.

🧠 O mercado reage antes do dinheiro chegar
O Fed não precisa literalmente “mandar dinheiro para o Bitcoin”. Muitas vezes, basta o mercado antecipar condições monetárias mais favoráveis para traders e investidores aumentarem exposição ao risco.

Mas existe um detalhe fundamental:
⚠️ Mais liquidez não significa alta garantida.
Inflação, juros, força do dólar, fluxos de ETFs, regulação, dados econômicos e sentimento de mercado continuam podendo mudar completamente o cenário.
A leitura mais correta é:
Mais liquidez costuma funcionar como vento favorável para a cripto — não como um botão automático de alta.
🔄 COMO ISSO PODERIA ACONTECER NA PRÁTICA?
Imagine este cenário:
O Fed aumenta a liquidez do sistema, os yields começam a aliviar e o mercado passa a enxergar menor pressão macroeconômica.
O capital pode começar a subir a escada de risco.
BTC normalmente tende a reagir primeiroBitcoin é a principal porta de entrada do mercado cripto. Quando o apetite por risco melhora, é comum que o BTC concentre primeiro os maiores fluxos.Depois o capital pode migrar para grandes altcoinsSe o BTC sobe de forma consistente e transmite confiança, ativos como ETH, SOL e BNB podem começar a receber uma parcela maior desse capital.Em seguida aparecem os ativos mais especulativosCom o mercado mais confiante, traders passam a procurar moedas de menor capitalização, narrativas emergentes e ativos com beta mais alto.
{spot}(BNBUSDT)
{spot}(ETHUSDT)
{spot}(BTCUSDT)

A sequência clássica seria:
Liquidez melhora → sentimento melhora → BTC sobe → grandes altcoins acompanham → capital começa a buscar ativos mais especulativos.
Ou, de forma simples:
BTC → Large Caps → Altcoins → Narrativas de maior risco
Mas o mercado não segue esse roteiro perfeitamente todas as vezes.
Às vezes o BTC sobe e as altcoins ficam paradas.
Em outros ciclos, a rotação demora semanas.
E também pode acontecer de o cenário macro melhorar, mas inflação, dólar forte ou realização de lucros travarem o movimento.
🎯 RESUMINDO
Liquidez é uma das variáveis macro mais importantes para acompanhar no mercado cripto.
Quando as condições financeiras melhoram, o BTC costuma estar entre os primeiros beneficiados. Se essa força continua, o capital pode se espalhar para altcoins — normalmente com movimentos maiores, tanto para cima quanto para baixo.
A pergunta importante não é apenas:
“O Fed está colocando mais liquidez no sistema?”
Mas também:
“Para onde esse dinheiro está indo?”
É aí que começa a diferença entre simplesmente acompanhar o mercado e entender a rotação de capital.
